a_rows_sample.anchor: AGM Postulates: Closure, Success, Consistency, Extensionality, Recovery ... K \circ p = Revision(K,p) ... K-p=Contraction(K,p) ... Lifecycle \supseteq \{Revision,Contraction,Supersession,Retraction\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes AGM belief-revision theory (Gardenfors 1992 / Hansson 1999) as third-priority reading for the Lifecycle TODO, giving candidate operators K∘p (Revision) and K-p (Contraction) and the five AGM postulates (Closure, Success, Consistency, Extensionality, Recovery), with Lifecycle ⊇ {Revision, Contraction, Supersession, Retraction}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: new facts can invalidate previous beliefs... Bird(Tweety) => Flies(Tweety) ... Emu(Tweety) causes the previous conclusion to be withdrawn
b_rows_sample.statement: Nonmonotonic reasoning (classical Tweety/Emu example) is established as a legitimate formal phenomenon relevant to the unresolved lifecycle/retirement/supersession TODO (distinguishing contradiction, revision, supersession, retirement, expiration): K_t |= p does not imply K_{t+1} |= p after new information arrives, i.e. Entailment at t != Permanent validity. The book gives the phenomenon and formalisms (e.g. default logic) but not KnowledgeOS's own lifecycle semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t^{I,\mathcal S}\models\alpha ... K_{t+1}^{I,\mathcal S'}\models\alpha ... Current\ derivability \neq permanent\ epistemic\ standing
b_rows_sample.statement: Not every reasoning regime is monotonic; defeasible/nonmonotonic reasoning (classical bird/emu withdrawal pattern) means K_t^{I,S} |= alpha does not establish K_{t+1}^{I,S'} |= alpha, i.e. current derivability != permanent epistemic standing — a formal research basis for revision, retraction and supersession, though it does not yet define the KnowledgeOS lifecycle relation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C(x):D(x) / E(x) ... Problem: Precedence of more specific defaults over more general ones must be handled ... Default reasoning provides the formal basis for: Defeasible inheritance, Nonmonotonic reasoning, Lifecycle/retirement semantics
b_rows_sample.statement: DL default rule (C(x):D(x) / E(x), i.e. if C(a) believed and D(a) consistent, conclude E(a)), with the specificity-precedence problem noted; claimed by the extraction to give KnowledgeOS a formal basis for defeasible inheritance, nonmonotonic reasoning, and lifecycle/retirement semantics.

Circumscription: Minimize abnormality ... Autoepistemic Logic ... K_t\models p\not\Rightarrow K_{t+1}\models p ... Lifecycle \supset Nonmonotonicity

Note: Candidate formal framework (Gardenfors/Hansson AGM postulates: Closure, Success, Consistency, Extensionality, Recovery) proposed for the open KnowledgeOS Lifecycle TODO, giving Lifecycle ⊇ {Revision, Contraction, Supersession, Retraction}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AAG=(V,E) ... V=V_C∪V_K∪V_I∪V_E∪V_T∪V_F
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Architecture Assurance Graph AAG=(V,E) with node types V_C (components/bounded contexts), V_K (contracts), V_I (invariants), V_E (enforcement mechanisms), V_T (verification tests), V_F (evidence/artifacts), and typed edges Component-owns->Invariant, Contract-carries->SemanticProperty, Mechanism-enforces->Invariant, Test-verifies->Invariant, Evidence-supports->Test/Claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I -> Owner -> Mechanism -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: For a critical property I, the complete assurance chain is I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence; a missing edge is potentially an assurance gap. Worked example: I_Authority->Governance->AuthorizationPolicy->NegativeTest->TestEvidence is a complete chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A — Defined and enforced ... D — Claimed but unverifiable
a_rows_sample.statement: Every invariant is classified into one of four situations: (A) defined and enforced and verified; (B) defined but not enforced (M=empty); (C) implemented but not architecturally declared (a mechanism exists but nobody established which invariant it protects); (D) claimed but unverifiable (documentation asserts I=True but no evidence exists). D is flagged as particularly dangerous.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I) ... Gap(I) in {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines assurance gap conceptually as Gap(I)=RequiredAssurance(I)-ActualAssurance(I), explicitly refusing to assign arbitrary numerical values and instead classifying into {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} 'until we establish a justified scoring model'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Component correctness =/=> System correctness
a_rows_sample.statement: An architecture may have every individual bounded context (Evidence, Assessment, Governance) correct while still having a critical global assurance gap, e.g. if the contract Assessment->Governance silently drops uncertainty; boxed conclusion: component correctness does not imply system correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assurance(I_global) <= min{Assurance(I_1),Assurance(I_2),...}
a_rows_sample.statement: States a weakest-link property: for a critical end-to-end property I_global, assurance is bounded by the minimum assurance of its constituent links, explicitly qualified as 'not a universal mathematical law; it is a useful conservative assurance model' — if one indispensable boundary lacks a provenance guarantee, end-to-end provenance cannot be honestly claimed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Traceability_syntactic=True but Traceability_historical=False
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision traceability example D->A->E: traceability is only True if each reference (Decision->Assessment ID->Evidence ID) remains resolvable and semantically versioned; if the Assessment ID resolves only to the latest Assessment, syntactic traceability can hold while historical traceability fails — 'this distinction is crucial'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SyntacticCorrectness =/= SemanticCorrectness ... HTTP 200 ... JSON schema valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes SyntacticCorrectness != SemanticCorrectness: an HTTP 200 proves transport success but not BusinessMeaningCorrect; a valid JSON schema does not prove SemanticContractValid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate six-dimension KnowledgeOS assurance vector A=(A_s,A_m,A_e,A_t,A_p,A_g): A_s structural (component exists, boundary explicit, dependencies controlled, contracts defined), A_m semantic (meaning preserved, no overloaded concept, no Boolean replacing a richer state), A_e epistemic/statistical (evidence, inference, assumptions, uncertainty, correlation vs causation, model version), A_t temporal (which version/policy/model applied when, historical reconstructability), A_p provenance (claim origin, traversable chain), A_g governance (who was authorized, under which valid policy, permission vs execution).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues a single global assurance score is dangerous: if A_s=1 but A_p=0, a scalar like 0.83 could falsely imply reasonable assurance, whereas for critical systems one missing indispensable property may be enough to block certification; boxed principle: vector assurance is preferable to premature scalarization — an explicit statistical-design principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C0 — Informational ... C4 — Critical assurance
a_rows_sample.statement: Provisionally classifies invariant criticality into five levels: C0 Informational (documentation/style), C1 Functional (normal business behavior), C2 Semantic (meaning/context preservation), C3 Governance (authority/policy/compliance), C4 Critical assurance (safety, irreversible action, high-impact decision, legally significant state); flagged as needing later validation against real KnowledgeOS use cases.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mechanism(I)=f(Criticality(I))
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes assurance-mechanism selection as a function of criticality: low-risk -> Documentation+UnitTest; medium -> IntegrationTest+ContractTest; high -> PropertyBasedTest+Replay+AuditEvidence; critical -> FormalModel/Proof where practical — self-labeled 'a proposed framework, not yet a frozen standard'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an AI-generated-artifact metadata schema A=(InputRef,ModelRef,InstructionRef,Output,Uncertainty,Validation,Provenance), stating the schema must be derived from the actual KnowledgeOS implementation but conceptually AI output should not be treated as an unexplained opaque fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI -> CandidateResult -> DeterministicValidation -> AcceptedArtifact. Not: AI -> ProductionTruth
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architecture must route AI output through AI->CandidateResult->DeterministicValidation->AcceptedArtifact, never directly AI->ProductionTruth, calling this distinction 'central to our KnowledgeOS design'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TrustedFor(x,p,t) ... Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose)
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns against another bare Boolean (`trusted = true`); trust/assurance must be contextual, TrustedFor(x,p,t) — an artifact trustworthy for Task_1 need not be trustworthy for Task_2. Generalizes to Valid(x) being usually incomplete; the better form is Valid(x,Context,Time,Purpose), called 'a major insight for KnowledgeOS': validity is not absolute but ValidForPurpose(P).

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralValid ... SemanticValid ... EpistemicallyValid ... TemporallyValid ... GovernanceValid
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five validity types (Structural/Semantic/Epistemic/Temporal/Governance Valid), concluding Valid(x) should be treated as shorthand only when the intended dimension is explicitly known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Different missing edges represent different classes of architectural weakness
a_rows_sample.statement: States the missing-node principle: Invariant->Owner with no Enforcement is a design gap; Enforcement->Test missing is an assurance gap; Test->Evidence missing is an auditability gap — different missing edges are different classes of architectural weakness, letting the architecture 'diagnose itself' via forall I_i: Complete(AAG(I_i))? producing a reproducible gap report.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System -> Output + EvidenceOfCorrectness
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the architecture's strongest form as System->Output+EvidenceOfCorrectness rather than merely System->Output, stated as precisely what deterministic assurance is trying to accomplish.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We should not claim: 'The architecture is mathematically proven.' ... FormalizableArchitecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-warning: the architecture must not be claimed as mathematically proven; what exists is a FormalizableArchitecture, and the next task is determining which portions can actually be Formalized->Specified->Verified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### DDD ... VERY STRONG ... Gītā 1–4 ... DEEP CONSISTENCY
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 211 verdict: DDD, Mathematics, Statistics, Governance, and AI are each rated VERY STRONG, and Gita chapters 1-4 rated DEEP CONSISTENCY, citing continued distinctions Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Action, Capability!=Authority, PastState!=CurrentState, Decision!=Outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prior-family acknowledgement in Step 209: NONE. ZERO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-i): machine grep of Step 209 for the corpus's prior invariant-naming families (INV-n, AFR-0n, GT-0n, GG-/GE-/GC-/GA-, IR-0n, CM-0n, LA-0n, AAI, PLP, and bare C1-C7/S1-S6/K1-K7/V1-V10/I1-I20) finds zero matches of any kind; Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208, in its opening line) and nothing else. The prior families are independently confirmed present and locatable in the corpus (AFR-0* in 3 files, INV-1* in 1, GT-0* in 1, AAI in 2, PLP in 1, IR-0* in 1, CM-0* in 1, LA-0* in 1); none is reconciled, mapped, superseded, or mentioned. Also uncited: Step 048 (global invariants), Step 092 (invariant preservation), Step 025N (a prior 'algebra' -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra), Step 091 (safety/liveness ground for Step 209's own Sections 209.35-37).

b_rows_sample.anchor: IS IT AN ALGEBRA? NO.
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-ii): an algebra requires a carrier set, closed operations, and laws. Step 209 supplies none of the three properly: the carrier ('an invariant') is never typed and is used interchangeably as a predicate on states (I(s)), a proposition (I_1 ∧ I_2), and a named object (I_identity) within one file; the only operation is unqualified conjunction (I_global = AND of I_i), imported from propositional logic and never defined on the carrier; no laws are stated (no associativity, commutativity, identity element, closure, absorption, or distributivity). The only other algebraic-looking object, A = {C,I,S,T,R} (Section 209.34), is ill-typed: written in set-brace notation for what the surrounding text treats as an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, so it cannot support the componentwise access the text assumes. Verdict: Step 209 is a taxonomy plus a conjunction, mislabelled an algebra -- a useful, well-organised three-level taxonomy of invariants (local/context/system), not an algebra.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Satisfiability is declared and never tested
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.32 declares that I_global = AND(I_1..I_n) 'is only valid if the invariants are jointly satisfiable' and states SAT(I_1 ∧ I_2 ∧ ... ∧ I_n) 'is an important next mathematical direction' but never tests it: COMPUTABILITY verdict DEFINED, not CONSTRUCTIBLE (the I_i are natural-language predicates, not formulas in any decidable logic), not COMPUTED, not TESTED. Section 209.33 constructs a hypothetical unsatisfiable pair (Action->Approval vs Action->ImmediateExecution) and does not check it against the actual I_KOS set.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
b_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: I_L(A), I_C(BC), I_S(System); Execution cannot manufacture authority; Semantic Laundering; I_KOS 8-set
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 ('Invariant Algebra') stratifies invariants into local/context/system levels (I_L, I_C, I_S); defines Verified(E)⇒Provenance(E)∧Integrity(E), Valid(A)⇒EvidenceBasis(A)∧ModelVersion(A), Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D), Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X) boxed as 'Execution cannot manufacture authority'; an epistemic partial order and knowledge lattice; 'Semantic Laundering' (a downstream context losing provenance/uncertainty of an upstream claim and treating the result as stronger than warranted); 'Determinism != Correctness'; architecture-as-CSP A={C,I,S,T,R}; safety properties P1-P4 and liveness properties L1-L2; and the boxed 8-member frozen set I_KOS={I_identity,I_version,I_provenance,I_temporal,I_epistemic,I_authority,I_decision,I_execution}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR with one ILL-TYPED object
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 reframes scattered '!=' observations into a stratified system but does not resolve the SAT question it raises nor reconcile with any prior invariant family. CLEAR: the three-level stratification, Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X), semantic laundering, determinism!=correctness. ILL-TYPED: A={C,I,S,T,R} uses set-brace notation for an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, which has no positional structure though the surrounding text requires componentwise access. NOT_DEFINED: the type of 'an invariant' itself, used as a predicate on states, a proposition, and a named object within one file. INCOMPLETE: I_KOS's eight members are one-word labels with no formulas, unlike the file's own worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 209.32 (conjunction written as established, satisfiability tested after, never run)
b_rows_sample.statement: I_global = AND_{i=1}^n I_i (Section 209.32) is written as an established equality, and the satisfiability precondition (SAT test) is stated only afterward, as future work, never run. If the I_i are not jointly satisfiable then I_global is identically false and the boxed I_global = AND(I_KOS) is an assertion of contradiction. Everything downstream that treats I_global as a satisfiable target -- Step 210's matrix, Step 211's AAG, Step 212's gap register -- is conditional on repairing this. Secondary: Section 209.14's determinism claim (SameState+SameCommand⇒SameDomainResult) is used inconsistently as assumption, requirement, and derived property without saying which.

b_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
b_rows_sample.statement: I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is DEFINED; I_KOS's 8 members are DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (unformalized); SAT(I_1∧...∧I_n) and SAT(A) are DEFINED but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (natural-language predicates, no decidable-logic encoding, and A is ill-typed); P1-P4/L1-L2 are DEFINED, self-described as 'candidates, not yet final requirements'; delta(A_t,c), Pre, Post are DEFINED with no aggregate instantiated. The file's own Section 209.34 concedes 'this is not yet a complete formal verification system.' Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED -- P1-P4 are called 'excellent candidates for deterministic assurance tests', none written or run.

b_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: MIXED with a good refusal and a violation
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's separation of probabilistic inference from deterministic governance (Section 209.15), Determinism!=Correctness (Section 209.16), InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence (Section 209.17, a genuinely important distinction between model misspecification and wide posteriors), HighUncertainty!=KnownIncorrect / LowUncertainty!=GuaranteedTrue (Section 209.18), and ObservedCorrelation⇏Causation (Section 209.29, uncited against Step 074) are all statistically correct. Measurement: Section 209.21 correctly declines to universalize a total order on epistemic strength (Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported, 'should not be interpreted as a universal total ordering') -- a good refusal -- but Section 209.25 then writes S(T(x))>S(x), a strict comparison requiring exactly the order just declined, four pages later with no reconciliation. KnowledgeState=(EvidenceStrength,Consistency,Uncertainty) is correctly presented as a partial order/lattice admitting incomparable elements, with no arithmetic attempted (correct). I_global=AND(I_KOS) conjoins a nominal set of one-word labels that are not propositions -- a type gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG on structure, WEAK on consistency boundaries; UL: 'Semantic Laundering' the best-defined new term
b_rows_sample.statement: The I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is textbook-correct and the clearest statement of the aggregate/context/system-invariant distinction in the corpus; Section 209.6 correctly identifies Decision.AssessmentRef⇒Resolvable(AssessmentRef) as crossing aggregates, but DDD's standard remedy (a consistency-boundary decision -- strong vs eventual consistency, process manager/saga) is never offered, despite the corpus already containing '# Step 166 — Process Managers, Sagas' (uncited). 'Semantic Laundering' (Section 209.24: 'a downstream context loses the provenance or uncertainty of an upstream claim and treats the transformed result as stronger than its source warrants') is judged the single best-defined new term in the band; against this, I_KOS's eight members enter the language as labels without definitions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS: conjunction cannot express the dependency graph the file itself draws
b_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: invariants are propositions closed under AND; a single global conjunction is the right composition; governance transitions can be made deterministic. Hidden: that conjunction is the only composition operator needed, despite Section 209.31's dependency graph showing invariants depending on one another (a relation AND cannot express) -- Sections 209.31 and 209.32 are structurally inconsistent, a dependency graph is not a flat conjunction (Internal Contradiction #B); that the I_i are mutually independent, contradicted by 209.31; that I_KOS's eight members cover the space, with no completeness argument (Step 210 immediately produces 15). Undefined symbols: Integrity(E), EvidenceBasis(A), AssessmentMethod(A), DecisionBasis(D), ApplicablePolicy(D), Resolvable(.), Traceable(D,Basis(D)), Basis(D), S(x), EvidenceStrength/Consistency components, Eventually(.), and every member of I_KOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 209
b_rows_sample.statement: Survives: the three-level invariant stratification; Semantic Laundering; Determinism!=Correctness; InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence; Execution cannot manufacture authority; identity continuity independent of state continuity; the safety/liveness lens; the insight that a constitution should constrain invariants, not technologies. Does not survive: the title (it is not an algebra); A={C,I,S,T,R} as typed; SAT(A) as computable; I_global=AND(I_KOS) as a verified-satisfiable object (unverified, and structurally at odds with the dependency graph of Section 209.31); S(T(x))>S(x) as a well-formed comparison.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Evidence/Test ordering is reversed between files, and Step 210's own boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own tuple
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's tail agenda for 210 orders Invariant->Owner->EnforcementPoint->Test->Evidence->FailureMode; Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple orders enforcement, monitoring, test, failure (test before the implied evidence); but Step 210's own boxed Section 210.40 conclusion states Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance (evidence before test); Step 211 Section 211.2 (boxed) and Step 214 Section 214.2 (boxed) both revert to Test before Evidence. Four sources agree that Test precedes Evidence; Step 210's one boxed conclusion disagrees with all of them, including with its own tuple -- the direction matters (Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test; Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout). This is Contradiction #5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
b_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.statement: Six further open questions: MQ-2 who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole, given three authority systems none of which spans them (sponsor+DA+ARB jointly); MQ-3 is N-1's breach to be repaired or is the invariant wrong (ARB); MQ-4 is PD-3's individual ownership intentional/a succession risk (DA); MQ-5 under M-A is the harvest responsibility (R-6) even required, since a reuse loop may be out of mission if the platform serves one product (ARB); MQ-6 does N-10 still hold or has evidence of insufficiency accumulated (ARB); MQ-7 what would falsify M-A, since a mission with no falsifier is not a mission (sponsor).

b_rows_sample.statement: Three independent proofs that D-1..D-7 do not belong in knowledge-types.yaml or bounded-contexts.yaml: (1) key collision, mechanical and decisive — bounded-contexts.yaml already contains a 'governance' key (product-side, code_path app/Contexts/Governance), so adding D-1 'Engineering Governance' would collide with an existing key in a lint-enforced enum; (2) vocabulary insufficiency, strong — the domain model's verbs (governs, produces, consumes, validates, derives, depends on, observes) have no expression in the edge vocabulary (depends_on, derived_from, verified_by), which lacks governs/produces/consumes/observes; (3) subject mismatch, strong — every L-A field is a property of a document (knowledge_id, last_review, code_refs), but 'Engineering Method' has no reviewer, next-review date, or code refs, so it cannot carry a knowledge card. Verdict: D-1..D-7 belong to L-B (which does not yet exist); expressing them as data would require a separate vocabulary file with its own enum namespace, an ARB decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The chain — tested, not assumed ... DESIGN POLICY (DP-n) ... ADMIT — DISCOVERED. Neither of us named it ... ENGINEERING DOMAIN owns Capability ... REJECT as an owner
b_rows_sample.statement: Testing the reviewer's proposed chain Mission->Strategy->Principles->Capability: ENGINEERING STRATEGY is admitted (12+ charter artifacts); ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE is admitted (six registers with own identifier series: AIP-01..14, AP-1..10, PGP-01..05, MC-01..08, SD-1..7, DR-1..8); DESIGN POLICY (DP-n) is discovered as a new anchor, since the Capability Catalog binds every capability to a DP (CAP-001->DP-1, etc.) and neither the reviewer nor the author had named it; 'Engineering Domain owns Capability' is rejected — no artifact links any CAP-n to a PD-n; the reviewer's concern that capabilities must not float is correct, but the repository already anchors them to DP-n, not to a domain. Chain: MISSION -> STRATEGY -> PRINCIPLE -> DESIGN POLICY -> CAPABILITY -> KNOWLEDGE -> ARTIFACT.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing concepts — recorded as hypotheses, not admitted (H-1..H-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate concepts recorded as hypotheses, none admitted: H-1 'I-12', a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads (n=1 capability, needs a second cross-boundary reader); H-2 Engineering Domain as owner of Capabilities (no artifact binds a CAP to a PD; DP-n already fills the slot); H-3 Knowledge Space nesting, does the EKP contain the PKS or sit beside it (containment vs adjacency unevidenced); H-4 whether OPERATIONAL-STATE attaches to the Artifact or the Knowledge it carries (would change I-1's granularity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 5 — D-3 · Amend the frozen Phase-02 map via AIP-13 (blocks the context-map section)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 5 (D-3): admit or reject the R-63/R-64 work-package/meta-governance boundary as a candidate context; dispose BC-5's dormancy. Recommendation: ADOPT the amendment procedure; within it, DEFER the new context per R-64's own bar and annotate BC-5 as dormant-observed. Authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 11 — Authorize the "KnowledgeOS Platform Architecture" workstream (NEW — packaged, deliberately NOT launched)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 11: whether to open a Phase-II Platform Architecture workstream (platform domains -> services -> responsibilities -> interactions -> capabilities -> execution assets; Core/Supporting/Generic; init->PKS flow). Opposing: (a) this IS Phase-C-class work and the B.5 gate's first door is D-9, which the same review says not to rush; (b) 'services' collides with the adopted N-10/Reference-Architecture stance against orchestrators/state machines unless the N-10 evidence bar clears; (c) launching another platform workstream while D-9 is unresolved is the exact AIP-14 exposure under examination. Risk of adopting now: the platform starts producing platform work 'until it exists for itself', ADR-AIP-02's own named failure mode. Recommendation: DEFER until D-9a/D-9b and the three doors resolve, then adopt as Phase C's operational-architecture view, with 'service' declared as responsibility-grouping unless the N-10 bar is separately cleared. Authority: ARB + sponsor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE DOMAIN ROW IS THE DISCOVERY OF THIS SECTION ... DOMAIN is a confirmed archetype with almost no outgoing edges ... ownership work is done by DP-n (governance-natured Knowledge), meaning work is done by Domains
b_rows_sample.statement: DOMAIN is confirmed as an archetype with almost no outgoing edges: it does not own capabilities (refuted), produce, constrain, or generate. What it does is scope meaning — it is the archetype of classification, not of ownership, which is orthodox strategic DDD empirically rediscovered (a subdomain never owns artifacts either; teams and contexts own things). Ownership work is done by DP-n (governance-natured Knowledge); meaning work is done by Domains. The reviewer's hierarchy places Domain as an owner in a stack; the evidence says it is a boundary-drawer standing beside the stack.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The hierarchy hypothesis — TESTED AND REFUTED AS A SINGLE STACK ... one supported edge, one refuted edge, four unevidenced. The single stack does not exist
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed single stack Purpose->Knowledge->Domain->Capability->Process->Runtime->Artifact is tested edge by edge: Purpose-above-all is supported; Knowledge->Domain has no evidence in either direction; Domain->Capability is already refuted (DP-n owns capabilities, not domains); Capability->Process has no evidence (if anything the arrow points the other way); Process->Runtime is inverted-ish (the runtime hosts the work); Runtime->Artifact holds only as containment of configuration artifacts. Verdict: one supported, one refuted, four unevidenced — the single stack does not exist. Collapsing four distinct orders into one stack is level mixing, a fourth instance of that error class in the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Objective 1 — Stable strategic domains? NO NEW STABLE STRATEGIC DOMAIN IS EVIDENCED
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate domains tested against Round47-OP's admissible-justification list: Bootstrap/Genesis fails (one criterion, n=1, not a domain); Engineering Governance already exists (a Supporting Subdomain); Knowledge Validation is not a domain but a capability family (H-CAT-1 already refused the parent abstraction); Runtime Integration is not a domain but a supporting subsystem+ACL, n=1 runtime; PKS Generation is merely an observation (n=0, never existed); Operational Learning is not a new domain but an existing mechanism governed in six places with 0 traversals. No new stable strategic domain is evidenced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O-1..O-24 (repository facts — no interpretation)
b_rows_sample.statement: 24 repository observations are recorded, each traced to a source artifact and kept strictly separate from interpretation. Key ones: O-1/O-2/O-3/O-4 (a 'Platform != product' table already classifies KnowledgeOS as potential product, Supporting Subdomain, and states the product binds the platform, never forks it); O-9 (an observed promotion model, itself a candidate for promotion); O-12 (Operational Evidence's owner recorded as 'the producing track; consumed by DA', lifecycle append-only, never edited); O-13 (a standing STOP forbidding a context map until operational evidence and an ARB ruling exist); O-16..O-18 (the Product Discovery Charter's five gated stages, PROPOSED status, one retrospective data point/zero market data points); O-20 (cross-product-research resolves to PENDING, no root); O-21 (CAP-001's Domain/Application/Shared contain zero repository knowledge); O-24 (CAP-001's evidence record holds four rows, zero tool executions, zero decisions changed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-01: the HANDOFF token's tokenRef acted as the de-facto knowledge channel and taught a lane the superseded path. A lane was taught the old path by its workflow record's tokenRef.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-5/F-5a: BC-7's HANDOFF tokenRef is performing de-facto knowledge distribution it does not own, evidenced by EKS-01 where a lane was taught a superseded path via its own workflow record's tokenRef -- the strongest evidence for a distinct C-10 (Knowledge Distribution) capability rather than 'Communication' in the ordinary sense.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
a_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Distinguish, explicitly: ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified. Receipt is not proof of application or compliance.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's knowledge-distribution lifecycle is to be modelled as seven distinguished states (ContextPublished, ContextSelected, ContextDelivered, ContextAvailable, ContextAcknowledged, ContextApplied, ContextVerified); a receipt is never proof of application or compliance, only of a narrower claim.

type_signature.codomain: one of seven distinguished lifecycle states

a_rows_sample.anchor: that recurrence is itself evidence bearing on C-10 -- governed knowledge arriving outside the governed channel -- and the analysis may note it, but per AMD1 must not assume C-10 owns it.
a_rows_sample.statement: A pattern of substantive external input (a cited review, a 925-line brainstorming document, external research) repeatedly arriving outside the governed channel is recorded as evidence potentially bearing on C-10, but explicitly not assumed to be owned by C-10 without further decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-10 is NOT the whole path. Its smallest coherent boundary is APPLICABILITY + RECEIPT. ... What nothing owns is: (a) deciding WHICH governed knowledge is applicable to THIS assignment, and (b) evidencing that the executing session actually holds the CURRENT version.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's smallest coherent capability boundary is proposed to be applicability determination plus receipt (not the whole created->published->selected->retrieved->delivered->acknowledged->applied->verified path), since creation/publication is BC-1's, retrieval/bootstrap is BC-6's, and only applicability-determination and receipt-evidencing are genuinely unowned.

a_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
a_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

a_rows_sample.anchor: receipt <= application <= understanding <= compliance ... A receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged. ContextApplied and ContextVerified are different claims requiring different evidence, and no receipt can supply them.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10's seven-state receipt model is elaborated with an explicit ceiling: a receipt can only ever evidence ContextAcknowledged, never ContextApplied or ContextVerified, and OQ-J is reformulated from a yes/no 'is the receipt authoritative' question into five separately-tested claims (delivery, possession, applicability, execution, compliance authority), of which a receipt can carry at most the first two.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Option C binds the receipt to an act the estate has never performed, that nobody owns, and that the analysis says a receipt cannot carry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Option C for C-10 receipt semantics is found unsatisfiable as worded, because it would require the receipt to reference an 'applicability decision' (ContextSelected) that never occurs and has no owner in the estate -- the same referent-gap defect noticed independently in several later documents.

a_rows_sample.anchor: establishes an applicability reference -- a pointer to decision A. does NOT establish the correctness of applicability -- whether A was right. A pointer to a judgement is not an assertion that the judgement was sound.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-10 Decision 1 (Option C) resolves OQ-J's authority defect by distinguishing an applicability REFERENCE (a pointer, which the receipt may carry) from applicability CORRECTNESS (whether the referenced judgement was sound, which the receipt does not establish) -- 'AUTHORITY IS CLAIM-SCOPED' is recorded as the invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The decision commits the receipt to reference an applicability decision that the estate never produces. ... This is no longer an authority problem -- it is an existence problem about the referent.
a_rows_sample.statement: A distinct 'referent gap' (as opposed to the already-solved authority gap) is identified: the decided receipt is required to reference an applicability decision (ContextSelected) that the estate never actually produces and nobody owns, so a conforming receipt is not presently populatable -- left as PO/ARB's to decide (optional/null reference, vs. a standing obligation to build ContextSelected).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No typed KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt structure is adopted -- and, verified: no such type exists anywhere in the estate
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit confirmation that no typed receipt data structure (e.g. KnowledgeDeliveryReceipt) exists anywhere in the estate's code or docs; schema design is deferred to Architecture and is not created by this semantic decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommended: YES -- C-10 exists as a capability, with realization NONE and its outer boundary OPEN. The load-bearing argument is D1 itself. ... A decision fixing the authoritative claim boundary of C-10's artifact presupposes a subject for that artifact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governance recommends C-10 existence = YES, arguing that D1's decided receipt-claim boundary presupposes a subject for that claim, supported by a distinct reason to change, a distinct outcome, and two genuinely unowned stages sharing one purpose (applicability + receipt) -- this recommendation is later overturned by the PO/ARB (S0120 D2) as conflating a decided semantic with a performed capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Of five activities: one occurs and is owned elsewhere; four do not occur at all. Evidence of C-10 having occurred: none
a_rows_sample.statement: Applying the ten-question existence test to the estate's evidence: of C-10's five constituent activities (applicability, delivery, acknowledgement, claim-scoped receipt, invalidation/reconciliation), only one occurs and it is owned by other contexts (BC-6/BC-7), while four never occur at all and have no owner -- the counter-evidence supporting the later NOT YET ESTABLISHED verdict.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting the receipt as authoritative state would supply limb one of the estate's existence test. A decision framed as constitutive would decide existence by the back door -- which this act forbids. Framed as a boundary specification, it does not.
a_rows_sample.statement: A distinction between a 'constitutive' decision (which would establish existence as a side effect) and a 'boundary specification' decision (which defines a candidate scope without establishing existence) is drawn, warning that D3 must be framed as the latter to avoid silently satisfying the D2 existence test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C -- SPLIT. Fits every decided constraint. It matches OQ-J's 2-of-5 result ... applicability / transport / execution are already owned or already excluded
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommendation: Option C (SPLIT) for D3 -- C-10 would own only the receipt/attestation lifecycle and state (receipt identity, lifecycle state, invalidation, completeness), explicitly excluding applicability determination, delivery transport, session execution, identity binding, dispute adjudication, execution authority, and compliance/application.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four unowned capabilities (corrected state)
b_rows_sample.statement: Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Manifestation Pipeline: from intelligence → knowledge → decision → implementation → operational reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reinterprets the seven-chakra system's downward 'manifestation current' (thought -> consciousness -> vision -> words -> action -> physical reality, as described by the source book) as a KnowledgeOS pipeline, mapping chakras 7-1 to Intelligence/Purpose, Architecture/Vision, Language/Specification, Collaboration/Trust, Execution/Governance, Adaptation/Learning, Reality/Evidence respectively.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge without purpose becomes information accumulation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chakra 7 -> Intelligence & Purpose Layer / Strategic Intent Layer, questions ('Why does this knowledge exist? What problem are we solving? What future state do we want?'), a KnowledgeIntent schema (id, purpose, desired_future_state, stakeholders, constraints), example intent 'We need trustworthy AI-assisted software engineering.' Principle KOS-CH7-001 is the anchor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A vision must become structurally understandable before implementation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chakra 6 -> Architecture & Modeling Layer (Architecture Model, Context Map, Capability Model, Roadmap objects); worked example turning 'We need AI governance' into an AI Engineering Platform Architecture with Agents/Knowledge Manager/Verification Engine/Governance Layer. Principle KOS-CH6-001 is the anchor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Language is the compression algorithm between human intention and machine execution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chakra 5 -> Language & Specification Layer, equated to DDD ubiquitous language, ADRs, specifications, API contracts (objects: Glossary, ADR, OpenAPI, BDD Scenario, Decision Record); illustrates the failure mode where an architect says 'Knowledge sovereignty' and a developer cannot interpret it without a defined Term/Definition/Rules record. Principle KOS-CH5-001 is the anchor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge becomes valuable when trusted relationships can use it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chakra 4 -> Trust & Collaboration Layer, mapped to community, teams, reviewers, governance bodies, human-AI collaboration (objects: Contributor, Reviewer, Knowledge Owner, Approval Authority). Principle KOS-CH4-001 is the anchor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge must have operational consequences.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chakra 3 -> Execution & Governance Layer, mapped to Architecture Decision -> Work Item -> Implementation -> Verification (objects: Work Package, Task, Workflow, Policy, Gate). Principle KOS-CH3-001 is the anchor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge must evolve through experience.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chakra 2 -> Learning & Feedback Loop, warns that 'many knowledge systems fail' by creating knowledge without creating learning; maps Implementation -> Observation -> Feedback -> Improved Knowledge (objects: Observation, Metric, Experiment, Retrospective, Learning Record). Principle KOS-CH2-001 is the anchor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge without evidence is only intention.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chakra 1 -> Reality & Evidence Layer, the foundation layer, mapped to actual evidence (Code, System, Logs, Metrics, Tests, Production Behavior; objects: Evidence Artifact, Runtime Observation, Test Result, Deployment Record), explicitly distinguished from 'documents' and 'diagrams'. Principle KOS-CH1-001 is the anchor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD Lens | AI Engineering Lens | Knowledge Graph Lens
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides three separate 7-row comparison tables mapping each chakra layer to a DDD equivalent (Strategic Domain Purpose/Bounded Context Design/Ubiquitous Language/Team Interaction/Application Services/Domain Events-Learning/Domain Reality), an AI Engineering Platform equivalent (AI Mission/Agent Architecture/Prompt-Contract Language/Human-Agent Trust/Agent Execution/Evaluation Loop/Evidence Verification), and a Knowledge Graph equivalent (Intent/Concept/Semantic/Trust/Action/Feedback/Evidence Nodes-Edges).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A system that transforms human intent into trustworthy engineering reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes that the chakra lens gives KnowledgeOS 'a vertical transformation model' (Meaning -> Structure -> Language -> People -> Action -> Learning -> Reality), explicitly distinguished from the 'horizontal layers' of classical software architecture (UI/API/Domain/Database), and offers the anchor as what KnowledgeOS 'is trying to become.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: The first mapping was useful, but it made one mistake: it treated the consciousness traditions as if they described one vertical stack that could simply be renamed into KnowledgeOS layers.
a_rows_sample.statement: The author states the earlier 'chakra → knowledge layer' vertical-stack mapping was too simplistic and must be refined into a multi-lens model rather than a single renamed stack.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The chakra model can be used as a diagnostic vocabulary for different dimensions of systemic maturity and blockage.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demotes chakras from architecture to a diagnostic vocabulary for systemic knowledge health (Ground/Identity/Agency/Relationship/Expression/Insight/Integration, each with a stated question and a corresponding 'blockage' failure mode, e.g. Ground blockage -> unreliable evidence, Identity blockage -> semantic ambiguity), explicitly warning not to claim 'KnowledgeOS has seven chakras.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: The consciousness model is not one architecture. It is a multi-lens model of a living system: what exists, how it is perceived, how it is interpreted, how identity forms around it, how action follows, how feedback changes the system, and how the system can become aware of its own knowing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Central thesis: the consciousness/Sankhya source material should be read as a multi-lens reference model of a living system (existence, perception, interpretation, identity formation, action, feedback, self-awareness of knowing), not as one vertical architecture to be relabeled.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality is not knowledge about reality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ontology lens: derived from the Purusha/Prakriti/Mahat/Manas/Buddhi/Ahamkara evolution chain, the architectural principle 'reality is not knowledge about reality' is asserted as one of the most important principles for KnowledgeOS, with reality (things/events/relationships/states/phenomena) feeding observations which feed knowledge representations (concepts/models/claims/decisions/rules).

b_rows_sample.anchor: observation ≠ interpretation / interpretation ≠ inference / inference ≠ fact / testimony ≠ direct evidence / belief ≠ truth
b_rows_sample.statement: Epistemology lens: derives an epistemic pipeline REALITY -> {OBSERVATION, INFERENCE, TESTIMONY} -> INTERPRETATION -> CLAIM -> EVALUATION -> KNOWLEDGE STATE from the Sankhya perception/inference/testimony triad and the Manas(receive)/Buddhi(process,filter)/Ahamkara(I/mine perspective) chain, and asserts it must preserve five non-collapses (observation vs interpretation, interpretation vs inference, inference vs fact, testimony vs direct evidence, belief vs truth), stated to fit the earlier observation->evidence->assessment->decision discipline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: It means every knowledge system has a standpoint problem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Cognitive-architecture lens: reframes Manas/Buddhi/Ahamkara not as literal modules but as three functions (intake, reasoning/discrimination, standpoint/ownership/perspective/bias), yielding the principle that every knowledge system has a standpoint problem, connected to prior work on knower standpoint, imported assumptions, plural perspectives, semantic frames, and sovereignty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence Context / Interpretation Context / Semantic Context / Decision Context / Governance Context / Memory/Lineage Context / Reflection/Assurance Context
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD lens: applies DDD questions (responsibility, ownership of information, decisions, observation, change, authority) to each cognitive faculty (Manas/Buddhi/Ahamkara/Karmendriyas), proposing seven candidate bounded contexts (Evidence, Interpretation, Semantic, Decision, Governance, Memory/Lineage, Reflection/Assurance), explicitly noting the source itself does not assert these are bounded contexts -- this is the author's own derivation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Now KnowledgeOS becomes a cybernetic knowledge organism rather than a repository. ... the key state is not documents but current epistemic state, with continuous feedback.
b_rows_sample.statement: Cybernetics lens: models KnowledgeOS as a feedback loop (ENVIRONMENT -> OBSERVATION -> INTERNAL STATE -> {ASSESSMENT, MEMORY} -> DECISION -> ACTION -> ENVIRONMENT, with feedback), asserting the key architectural state is 'current epistemic state', not a document repository.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge content ≠ authority over knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Governance lens: from the Purusha (immutable, neither cause nor effect) vs Prakriti (changing field) distinction, derives the principle 'knowledge content is not authority over knowledge' -- KNOWLEDGE (claims/evidence/models/interpretations/decisions) must be separated from GOVERNANCE (who may assert/approve/change/invalidate/adjudicate); explicitly identified as the same sovereignty principle protected elsewhere in the project.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation, evidence, inference, confidence, authority and decision should remain orthogonal.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence/assurance lens: from the source's list of perception-failure causes (distance, subtlety, obstruction, indistinguishability, sensory faults, inattentive mind) derives an observation-reliability pipeline (source/conditions/completeness/reliability/uncertainty/perspective -> EVIDENCE -> Inference -> Assessment -> Decision, each stage carrying its own uncertainty), restating the orthogonality principle that observation, evidence, inference, confidence, authority and decision must remain orthogonal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpretation_t = f(Evidence_t, Knowledge_{t-1}) ... Knowledge is path-dependent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Temporal/lineage lens: reinterprets samskaras (impressions left by experience) as a feedback loop experience->memory->pattern->expectation->future interpretation, formalized as Interpretation_t = f(Evidence_t, Knowledge_{t-1}), asserting past knowledge is not passive and 'knowledge is path-dependent.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structure / Process / Development
b_rows_sample.statement: Architecture lens: separates what the first model conflated into three orthogonal aspects -- Structure (tattvas/koshas/faculties/chakras -- what the system is made of), Process (perception/interpretation/reasoning/action/feedback -- how it operates), and Development (practice/discipline/concentration/meditation/integration -- how it transforms), mapped respectively to KnowledgeOS ontology/contexts/entities/relationships, cognition/inference/decisions/feedback, and maturity/refinement/integration/learning.

b_rows_sample.anchor: META-COGNITION ... "How do I know this?" "What assumptions am I using?" "What evidence supports it?" "Where could I be wrong?" "Am I authorized to act?"
b_rows_sample.statement: AI-agent lens: enriches the plain prompt->LLM->tool->answer loop with a consciousness-derived structure (PERCEPTION/MEMORY -> MANAS-like intake -> REASONING/BUDDHI-like -> SELF/PERSPECTIVE -> DECISION -> ACTION -> OBSERVATION feeding back to memory) plus an added META-COGNITION layer asking self-examination questions, explicitly identified as where the project's verification engine, review engine, governance mechanisms and deterministic assurance become relevant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lens table: Ontology/Epistemology/Cognition/Perspective/DDD/Cybernetics/Governance/Evidence/Temporal/Architecture/Development/AI cognition
b_rows_sample.statement: Synthesis table pairing each of twelve lenses' 'consciousness question' with its 'KnowledgeOS question' (e.g. Ontology: What exists? -> What is the domain actually made of?; Governance: Who has authority? -> Who may assert/change/approve knowledge?), presented as the model the author would keep instead of a single mapping.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CONCRETE / OPERATIONAL / INTERPRETIVE / EXPLANATORY / INTEGRATED
b_rows_sample.statement: Recasts the five koshas (Annamaya/Pranamaya/Manomaya/Vijnanamaya/Anandamaya) as a depth-of-understanding maturity lens: CONCRETE -> OPERATIONAL -> INTERPRETIVE -> EXPLANATORY -> INTEGRATED, not a component architecture, noting the source places Vijnanamaya at the level where perception gains meaning through awareness/insight/consciousness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance discipline -> Knowledge structural discipline -> Noise reduction -> Focused investigation -> Continuous reasoning -> Integrated understanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Recasts Yoga's eight limbs (progressing from bodily/personality refinement toward senses, mind, higher consciousness) as a transformation lens for KnowledgeOS: Governance discipline -> Knowledge structural discipline -> Noise reduction -> Focused investigation -> Continuous reasoning -> Integrated understanding, described as closer to the project's existing knowledge workflow.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K + provenance(K) + uncertainty(K) + authority(K) ... a reflexive knowledge system additionally represents K + provenance + uncertainty + authority + perspective + history + assumptions + limitations + transformations, and can reason about its own epistemic state.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an escalating series of knowledge-system representational completeness: a normal system represents K; a better one represents K+provenance(K); a trustworthy one represents K+provenance+uncertainty+authority; a reflexive knowledge system additionally represents K+provenance+uncertainty+authority+perspective+history+assumptions+limitations+transformations and can reason about its own epistemic state -- posed as KnowledgeOS's target formulation ('KnowledgeOS is a reflexive knowledge system').

b_rows_sample.anchor: What happens when the system that knows becomes capable of examining how it knows? ... it should remain a reference model and diagnostic vocabulary, not become the architecture itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes with the open question 'what happens when the system that knows becomes capable of examining how it knows?' as the deepest connection to the KnowledgeOS program, paired with an explicit warning that the consciousness framework must remain a reference model and diagnostic vocabulary and never become the architecture itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: as a conceptual/epistemic analogy, not as a scientific claim that chakras physically exist or that knowledge literally has energy centres.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly frames the entire exercise as extracting an architectural pattern from the consciousness/chakra tradition as analogy, not asserting the tradition's mechanisms are literally real.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Purusha | epistemic witness / meta-awareness ... I would not say KnowledgeOS has a 'soul'. Instead: Purusha becomes a useful metaphor for the observing layer that can distinguish the knowledge system from the contents of the knowledge system.
b_rows_sample.statement: An 18-row correspondence table (Universe/Prakriti->knowledge environment, Senses->evidence acquisition, Nadis->information flows, Chakras->functional knowledge centres, Prana->epistemic flow, Manas->observation layer, Buddhi->reasoning, Ahamkara->perspective/bias, Samskaras->historical memory, Vasanas->persistent tendencies, Koshas->abstraction levels, Kundalini->progressive integration, Chakra blockage->knowledge debt/contradiction, Yoga->refinement practice, Dharana->focused investigation, Dhyana->sustained reasoning, Samadhi->integrated understanding, Purusha->epistemic witness/meta-awareness), with an explicit warning against reading Purusha as implying KnowledgeOS has a soul -- it is a metaphor for the layer distinguishing the knowledge system from its own contents.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A document is not knowledge. It is closer to sensory input. A statement inside it is not necessarily truth. It is an observation or claim.
b_rows_sample.statement: From the Manas(observation/capture)->Buddhi(interpretation/discrimination)->Ahamkara(perspective/ownership/bias)->Knowledge-State pipeline, derives the principle that a document is not knowledge but closer to sensory input, a statement inside it is an observation/claim rather than necessarily truth, and interpretation and perspective are separate operations layered on top.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What was observed? -> What was inferred? -> What assumptions entered? -> What perspective entered? -> What alternatives exist? -> What contradicts it? -> What survives examination?
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames critical thinking as the 'Buddhi-like' discrimination mechanism able to extract the state of knowledge, operationalized as a seven-question chain, and restates the Sankhya three-source-of-knowledge model (perception preferred, inference when perception insufficient, testimony when neither available) as an evidence pipeline: Direct observation / Inference / Authority-testimony -> Evaluation -> Knowledge State.

b_notations: K + provenance + uncertainty + authority + perspective + history + assumptions + limitations + transformations

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'sankhya-consciousness-multi-lens-reference-model' POSSIBLY relates to 'chakra-manifestation-pipeline' (batch B0013). Note: S0493's refinement of an earlier chakra=knowledge-layer vertical-stack mapping into a ten-lens reference model (ontology/epistemology/cognition/perspective/DDD/cybernetics/governance/evidence/temporal/architecture/development/AI-cognition) drawn from Sankhya/consciousness sources, culminating in a 'reflexive knowledge system' formulation; explicitly a diagnostic reference model, not architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governed knowledge-revision workflow versus naive automatic retraining
a_rows_sample.statement: Depicts a governed workflow Outcome -> Evaluation -> Error/Drift Detection -> Hypothesis -> Model Revision Candidate -> Validation -> Review/Approval -> New Model Version -> Future Decisions, contrasted as 'much safer than' a naive Outcome -> automatically retrain everything. Some low-risk updates may be automated; critical updates require HumanApproval, so LearningPolicy determines autonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Model promotion lifecycle, shadow mode, champion/challenger, multi-objective constrained model selection
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a model lifecycle Candidate -> Validated -> Approved -> Active -> Deprecated, resembling software deployment governance. A new model can run in ShadowMode (predicting without influencing decisions) to compare M_current vs M_candidate -- 'an excellent safety mechanism'. Defines Champion/Challenger: M_champion vs M_challenger, the challenger must demonstrate sufficient performance before replacing the champion, and performance is multidimensional (not just Accuracy but Calibration, Robustness, Fairness, Safety, Latency, Cost, Interpretability, domain-dependent). Formalizes multi-objective model selection M* = argmax_M Utility(M) subject to Safety(M), Calibration(M), Cost(M)<=C_max -- 'connects model evolution to constrained optimization'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 45 adaptive-learning model (all PASS)
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) new evidence contradicts an old interpretation => interpretation revised, original evidence unchanged; (2) a model becomes obsolete => historical decisions retain the old model version; (3) a new model performs better => does not automatically replace the active model unless promotion policy allows it; (4) input distribution changes but decision-relevant behavior does not => distribution drift recorded without declaring causal/model failure; (5) statistically significant drift has negligible operational impact => no automatic critical escalation from statistical significance alone; (6) a model predicts poorly despite good historical calibration => performance reevaluated, calibration alone does not protect the model; (7) a successful outcome follows a poor decision => outcome success does not automatically validate decision quality; (8) a justified decision produces an adverse low-probability outcome => not automatically classified as irrational; (9) a governance policy changes => future decisions use the new policy, historical decisions retain the old policy version; (10) a new interpretation of old evidence is created => both historical and current interpretations remain traceable; (11) a model trained on one bounded context detects drift => impact stays scoped to relevant contexts unless evidence supports broader generalization; (12) a candidate model performs well in shadow mode but violates a safety constraint => cannot be promoted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Champion/challenger adversarial review and a falsification budget
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends champion/challenger to epistemic control: an independent M_challenger should ideally use different assumptions, independent evidence, and different methodology; the challenger asks 'what would falsify the current conclusion' rather than 'can I support it', creating FalsificationPressure. Proposes a deliberate Budget_falsification: for critical decisions, resources should be reserved specifically to try disproving the preferred hypothesis, since a system optimized only for DecisionSuccess may stop searching once it finds supporting evidence, while one optimized partly for Falsification actively searches for failure modes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge maturity state machine: Raw->Candidate->Validated->Trusted->Operational, with Questioned/Invalidated demotion
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge moves through Raw -> Candidate -> Validated -> Trusted -> Operational (labels defined by policy); AI-generated information initially belongs to CandidateKnowledge, useful but Candidate != Trusted. Promotion requires Evidence and Validation and Scope and Freshness and NoCriticalConflict, formalized as a gate Promote(K). Knowledge must also move backward: Trusted -> Questioned -> Invalidated ('essential for self-correction'); depicts the full state machine Candidate->Validated->Trusted->Operational branching to Questioned->Invalidated or Deprecated, with transitions required to preserve provenance. Trusted does not mean eternal: a trusted claim can become Stale or Invalid, so Trusted is a current epistemic state, not a permanent property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic debt: unresolved conflicts, stale claims, unvalidated hypotheses -- analogous to technical debt, must be visible and scoped
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines EpistemicDebt as the accumulation of unresolved conflicts, stale claims, unvalidated hypotheses, missing evidence, and uncertain mappings -- 'analogous to technical debt'. An AI agent should be able to query EpistemicDebt(K,Context) before a high-impact decision; debt must be scoped, since a system may have low overall debt but high debt concentrated in one critical domain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Self-correction without automatic history rewrite; correction-quality recursion and validation stopping rule
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires ErrorDetected => CorrectionCandidate but explicitly not ErrorDetected => AutomaticHistoryRewrite. Depicts a correction loop: Prediction -> Observation -> Error Detection -> Root-Cause Analysis -> Correction Candidate -> Validation -> Promotion -> Future Prediction. Notes a correction can itself be wrong, so Correction is another hypothesis requiring validation, creating Claim -> Validation -> Correction -> Validation recursion needing a stopping criterion (else endless revalidation); the stopping rule is MarginalExpectedValue < Cost and DecisionRisk below acceptable limits -- 'connects again to VOI'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 47 epistemic-control model (all PASS)
b_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) KnowledgeOS strengthens a belief using evidence generated by its own previous policy => evidence dependency recognized; (2) the system converges on a stable but incorrect model => stability not interpreted as correctness; (3) a challenger model contradicts the champion => disagreement preserved and investigated; (4) new evidence reduces confidence => confidence can decrease; (5) a trusted claim becomes invalid => demoted without deleting its history; (6) an AI-generated hypothesis has no independent evidence => cannot automatically become operational knowledge; (7) a candidate learning policy would improve information gain but violate a safety constraint => safety blocks the exploration; (8) a model update improves average accuracy but violates a critical invariant => promotion rejected; (9) multiple validation results share the same underlying source => not counted as independent confirmation; (10) a historical interpretation is later disproven => historical decision remains reproducible using its original knowledge state; (11) the system's own policy changes the population from which evidence is collected => policy-induced distribution shift represented; (12) the model becomes increasingly confident while prediction error simultaneously increases => calibration/reality-gap mechanism flags epistemic instability or model failure.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledge-maturity-state-machine' POSSIBLY relates to 'champion-challenger-model-promotion-lifecycle' (batch B0023). Note: Step 47's knowledge-level (as opposed to model-level) maturity/promotion/demotion state machine plus the epistemic-debt concept (accumulated unresolved conflicts/stale claims/unvalidated hypotheses, analogous to technical debt) and the self-correction/recursive-validation loop with its VOI-linked stopping rule; parallels but is distinct from champion-challenger-model-promotion-lifecycle's model-level Candidate/Validated/Approved/Active/Deprecated lifecycle.

a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies two genuinely irreducible formal gaps (both graded G1): (1) Qualify has no executable/formal body, remaining the blocker for making πK computable — Sanjaya recovers the missing referent/observation layer (W,Ω,O) but does not solve Qualify; (2) three corpus equality relations (≡ semantic, ≈ observational, ≅_λ provenance-sensitive) lack decision procedures — equality is not missing as a concept but is under-specified as an executable formalism, and the research should not invent another equality relation to make D285-5 work.

a_rows_sample.statement: States the overall verdict and next research target: the three gap-update artifacts show real progress (moving from 'are we missing concepts?' to 'which recovered concepts are formally specified enough to support executable claims?'); the next target is not another Sanskrit hypothesis but formalizing the corpus equality relations and Qualify, kept strictly separate — this is where the investigation can either make πK computable or rigorously demonstrate why it cannot.

a_rows_sample.statement: Amendment 1: withdraws a citation that had claimed 'history ⊊ structural ⊊ semantic' as a corpus hierarchy — measurement shows this occurs only in verification-lane artifacts, while the corpus (location 246) defines exactly four non-interchangeable relations (structural =, semantic ≡, observational ≈, provenance-sensitive ≅_λ), and 'history' is not among them.

a_rows_sample.statement: Argues that any invariant comparing objects is relation-relative among the four equality relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ): a transformation can preserve semantic state (K_t ≡ K_{t+1}) while changing structurally (K_t ≠_structural K_{t+1}) because metadata/representation changed, and provenance-sensitive equality may distinguish states that semantic equality identifies.

a_rows_sample.anchor: under **structural equality**, the relevant antecedent can be false; under **semantic equality**, the witness becomes substantive, but only after choosing what semantics preserve; under **observational equality**, the result depends on the permitted observation set; under **provenance-sensitive equality**, the same witness can cease to establish non-injectivity. So **"equality" is not one mathematical operation in this programme.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Summarizes the D285-5 witness's behavior across all four equality relations as evidence that equality cannot be hand-waved: structural equality makes the antecedent false; semantic equality makes the witness substantive only after choosing what semantics preserve; observational equality's result depends on the permitted observation set; provenance-sensitive equality can make the same witness cease to establish non-injectivity — concluding 'equality' is not one mathematical operation in this programme but a family whose members must each be operationally decided.

a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the derivation that with a product state space, observational equality naturally becomes projection onto an axis subset X (Sigma_1 approx_X Sigma_2 iff pi_X(Sigma_1)=pi_X(Sigma_2)), so the axes themselves ARE the permitted observations — giving exactly 2^5=32 candidate relations forming a natural containment lattice (from ≈_∅, everything equal, to ≈_{A,S,R,V,C}, structural equality on Sigma); changes the target's status from an undefined normative parameter to a form-DERIVED relation with a bounded 32-option normative choice remaining.
