b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against stating an unsupported compliance percentage (e.g. '82% compliant') without first defining the requirement population, weighting, independence, evidence quality, confidence model and treatment of critical properties; recommends a qualitative CriticalGap measure instead.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G1 — Semantic gap ... G5 — Assurance gap ... These gaps can coexist
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five coexisting gap classes: G1 Semantic (software loses domain meaning), G2 Governance (authority/responsibility ambiguous), G3 Temporal (historical state not reconstructable), G4 Epistemic (evidence/uncertainty/assumptions lost), G5 Assurance (behavior may be correct but insufficiently evidenced).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Implementation = Present but Assurance = Weak. This is not necessarily an implementation gap. It is an: Assurance Gap
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example distinguishing implementation presence from assurance: modelVersion correctly stored (Implementation=Present) but with no automated test proving it survives the workflow (Assurance=Weak) is classified specifically as an Assurance Gap, not an implementation gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ArchitectureGap != ImplementationGap != VerificationGap
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Architecture gap (design itself lacks the mechanism), Implementation gap (mechanism specified but code does not implement it correctly), and Verification gap (implementation appears correct but evidence is insufficient) as three non-identical gap types.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing ... Ownerless Invariants ... Shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a governance gap pattern where a technical mechanism (AI->Assessment->Approval) works but nobody has defined who is authorized to approve, so TechnicalCapability=Present while GovernanceCapability=Missing; introduces the 'ownerless invariant' search (Owner(I)=empty set, dangerous because nobody maintains it) and its converse, the 'shared ownership' problem, where undivided shared responsibility (Owner(I)={A,B,C}) risks each team assuming another enforces the invariant -- boxed as 'shared responsibility must not mean undefined responsibility'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C) ... Loss(C)={p | p in CriticalProperties and p absent after transformation}
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-loss function for a context-to-context contract L(C)=InformationBefore(C)-InformationAfter(C), refined to Loss(C) as the set of critical properties absent after transformation; worked example: an Assessment=(score,uncertainty,modelVersion,evidenceRef) contract sending only {score} loses uncertainty/modelVersion/evidenceRef, a Critical Semantic Gap if downstream governance requires them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ΔT=T_target △ T_actual where △ denotes symmetric difference ... Unauthorized State Transition Path
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing actual state-machine transitions T_actual from implementation and comparing to target transitions T_target via symmetric difference DeltaT = T_target triangle T_actual as a state-transition gap measure; a transition present in T_actual but absent from T_target is an Unauthorized State Transition Path warranting high priority when governance consequences exist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t) ... Reproducibility ... Replayability ... A system may be replayable without being perfectly reproducible
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines historical replay Replay(A,t)=F(Data_t,Policy_t,Model_t,Schema_t,Context_t), noting exact replay (Replay(A,t)=A_t) may be impossible when external conditions change, in which case the system should preserve enough provenance to explain why; distinguishes Reproducibility (can we regenerate the same result, F(X,M)=Y again) from Replayability (can we reconstruct what happened and why), noting a system may be replayable without being reproducible (e.g. a now-defunct external service).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A new state does not necessarily know the old state ... CurrentState + HistoricalProvenance ... History must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a technically disciplined reading of an earlier 'Chapter 4' observation ('a new state does not necessarily know the old state'): rejects CurrentState=History, proposing instead CurrentState+HistoricalProvenance as sufficient for reconstructing relevant prior meaning; boxed principle: history must be preservable, not necessarily embedded in every current state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prediction -> AutomaticAuthority ... CurrentState -> AssumeCompleteHistory ... Unknown -> False ... Execution -> AssumeSuccess ... Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions
b_rows_sample.statement: States a negative-space design principle: a mature architecture must specify ForbiddenPaths as well as AllowedPaths (Architecture=AllowedTransitions+ForbiddenTransitions), and lists four named forbidden implicit transitions to guard against: Prediction->AutomaticAuthority, CurrentState->AssumeCompleteHistory, Unknown->False, Execution->AssumeSuccess.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assessment -/-> Authority ... The X is important. It represents a path that the architecture must prevent
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 211 Architecture Assurance Graph with an explicit forbidden-path marker: Evidence->Assessment->Governance->Decision->Authorized Action->Execution->Outcome, with an explicit forbidden edge Assessment-/->Authority that the architecture must prevent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G-01 Identity ... G-15 History ... This is the audit instrument
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 15-item provisional gap register (G-01 through G-15) as concrete audit questions (identity/state separation, historical reconstructability, provenance traceability, uncertainty preservation across boundaries, model/version provenance, inference-to-authority escalation, decision/execution separation, execution/outcome separation, illegal transition blocking, contract semantic loss, contradiction coexistence, unknown-vs-false distinguishability, automatic critical-invariant testing, single accountable ownership, prior semantic context reconstruction).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No evidence => Unknown. Not: No evidence => Missing. And certainly not: No evidence => Implemented
b_rows_sample.statement: States the methodological rule of Step 212 as most important: the gap register's rows must not be populated by imagination but from actual KnowledgeOS artifacts, with the default for absence of evidence being No evidence=>Unknown, explicitly not =>Missing and certainly not =>Implemented.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Architectural reasoning PASS ... Gītā Chapters 1–4 COHERENT
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 212 verdict: architectural reasoning, DDD, mathematics, statistics, and AI dimensions each rated PASS; Gita chapters 1-4 rated COHERENT (continuing to generate architectural questions without being presented as technical proof).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 5 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

a_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
a_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

a_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
a_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R_i=(S_i,A_i,O_i,F_i,H_i,E_i,D_i,P_i,I_i,V_i,U_i) ... deliberately redundant ... prevents us from collapsing different kinds of knowledge into one field called 'conclusion'
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an 11-field master reconstruction record R_i (Step, Artifact, Observation, established Fact, Hypothesis, Experiment, Derivation, Proposal, Invariant, Verification, Unresolved uncertainty) per meaningful unit in Steps 1-182, deliberately redundant to prevent collapsing distinct knowledge kinds into one generic 'conclusion' field.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lossless extraction -> later compression. Not: Compression -> hope nothing important was lost ... ApparentlyIrrelevant(t_i) does not imply ArchitecturallyIrrelevant(t_i)
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires the first reconstruction pass to be lossless (preserving terminology, competing interpretations, failed approaches, corrections, examples, objections, uncertainty) rather than aggressively summarized, on the grounds that apparent irrelevance does not imply architectural irrelevance -- a rejected idea may later explain why a boundary exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Only after extraction should Claude normalize terminology ... do not merge automatically. First ask: SameMeaning? If uncertain: Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires a second, semantic-normalization pass performed only after lossless extraction, mapping Term_i to Concept_j only after explicitly checking SameMeaning and defaulting to Unknown when uncertain rather than auto-merging.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Term_A -> Term_B -> Term_C ... merely editorial refinement; a change in understanding; discovery of a more precise distinction ... Concept genealogy
b_rows_sample.statement: States that terminology drift across the 182 steps is itself evidence (possibly editorial refinement, changed understanding, or discovery of a finer distinction) and must be retained rather than silently normalized away; introduces 'concept genealogy' (C_0->C_1->C_2->C_3, asking where a concept first appeared and when its meaning materially changed) as potentially one of the most valuable reconstruction outputs, illustrated by a candidate genealogy Initial Problem->Ad-hoc Rule->Repeated Failure->Explicit Constraint->Invariant->Architecture Constitution->Automated Assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Emergence(I) ≠ Formalization(I). And: Formalization(I) ≠ Implementation(I). And: Implementation(I) ≠ Verification(I) ... Implicit -> Recognized -> Named -> Formalized -> Implemented -> Verified
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-stage distinction (Emergence != Formalization != Implementation != Verification) to be maintained throughout the reconstruction, refined into a six-stage invariant lifecycle (Implicit->Recognized->Named->Formalized->Implemented->Verified) with the explicit note that not every invariant reaches every stage; illustrated by tracing Unknown!=False from an informal complaint through naming, formalization as a three-valued KnowledgeState enum, implementation, and verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Origin -> Motivation -> Definition -> Derivation -> Application -> Validation ... prevents 'mathematical decoration' ... What engineering decision does it influence? If there is no answer ... the formula may belong in a theoretical appendix
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires tracing every mathematical construct through Origin->Motivation->Definition->Derivation->Application->Validation to prevent 'mathematical decoration' (formulas added after the fact with no engineering problem behind them); defines a formula-audit checklist (symbol definitions, stated assumptions, classification as definition/identity/derivation/model/approximation/empirical-relation/heuristic, and which engineering decision it influences), demoting any formula with no engineering-decision answer to a theoretical appendix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EmpiricalDistribution ... TheoreticalDistribution ... F-hat_n(x) ... is an empirical distribution function. It describes observed data. It is not automatically evidence that the underlying population has a particular theoretical distribution
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires distinguishing empirical distribution (observed data, e.g. the empirical CDF) from theoretical distribution and observed data from a random-variable model, since an empirical distribution function does not automatically evidence any particular underlying theoretical distribution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservedArtifacts -> LatentArchitecturalModel ... P(A|O) ∝ P(O|A)P(A) ... The architecture we reconstruct is an inference from evidence, not direct observation of an abstract whole
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames architecture reconstruction as a latent-structure statistical inference problem (P(Architecture|ObservedArtifacts) proportional to P(Observed|Architecture)*P(Architecture)), explicitly not requiring literal Bayesian implementation but establishing that the reconstructed architecture is an inference from evidence, not a direct observation, and therefore carries confidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If two architectural interpretations explain the evidence equally well ... we should retain both as candidates ... Architectural Underdetermination ... This is not failure. It is a legitimate knowledge state
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Architectural Underdetermination as a legitimate knowledge state (when available evidence is compatible with multiple architectural interpretations, both should be retained as candidates rather than one being forced true); requires an uncertainty register (ID, question, competing interpretations, evidence, resolution status) to prevent unresolved questions disappearing during synthesis, and requires confidence to be attached per-claim rather than as a global architecture-wide percentage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: G=(V,E) ... V={Artifact,Observation,Fact,Hypothesis,Experiment,Decision,Principle,Invariant,Architecture,Test} ... the KnowledgeOS Evidence Graph
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the KnowledgeOS Evidence Graph G=(V,E) with a ten-type node vocabulary and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, implements, verifies, supersedes), extended with time-stamped nodes/edges (t_start, t_end) so historical validity (Valid(C,t)) becomes a first-class graph property.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 -[superseded]-> C_2. Not: delete(C_1) ... Deprecated ... Falsified ... Deprecated ≠ Falsified. A technology choice may be deprecated because circumstances changed. The original choice may still have been correct at the time
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes supersession (recorded as an edge, never deletion) from deletion, and Deprecated (no longer preferred/applicable) from Falsified (evidence demonstrates incorrectness under stated assumptions), arguing the book must evaluate historical decisions using their contemporaneous context rather than portraying every superseded choice as an error -- termed 'architectural fairness'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A*_t = argmax_A U(A | Information_t) ... A*_{t+1} ≠ A*_t. This is not necessarily inconsistency. It is learning ... Architecture evolution is: the controlled transformation of architectural decisions in response to changing evidence, constraints and knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes contextual rationality (A*_t=argmax U(A|Information_t), such that a later optimal choice under new information differing from an earlier one is learning, not inconsistency) and redefines architecture evolution as the controlled transformation of architectural decisions in response to changing evidence, constraints and knowledge, rather than merely 'new technology replaced old'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preserve distinctions; preserve lineage; preserve uncertainty ... A knowledge-centric software architecture should preserve the distinctions, lineage and uncertainty required to interpret information correctly across time, context and authority boundaries ... Critical(K) ⊆ Preserved(T(K))
b_rows_sample.statement: States the candidate unifying meta-principle for the whole book (preserve distinctions, lineage, uncertainty, appearing across DDD, statistics, mathematics, AI, governance, temporal modeling, architecture, and the Gita reflections), formalized over a knowledge state K=(content,context,temporal-validity,provenance,epistemic-state) as Critical(K) subset-of Preserved(T(K)) for any architectural transformation T.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Semantic Preservation Principle ... P_critical(K) => P'_critical(T(K)) ... If a transformation intentionally removes a property, that loss must be: explicit; documented; justified; visible to downstream consumers
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the Semantic Preservation Principle (for any transformation T, critical semantic properties must not be silently lost, P_critical(K)=>P'_critical(T(K))) as a candidate core architectural law of KnowledgeOS, requiring any intentional property removal to be explicit, documented, justified, and visible to downstream consumers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI transformations are particularly dangerous because ... can silently remove: uncertainty; provenance; alternatives; context; temporal validity ... What information did the transformation preserve, transform or lose?
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Semantic Preservation Principle specifically to AI transformations (Input->Interpretation->Summary->Recommendation), arguing AI operations must be treated as semantic transformations T_AI whose relevant question is not whether the answer is good but what information was preserved, transformed, or lost; defines an AI semantic-loss audit (Loss_semantic=CriticalAttributes_in minus CriticalAttributes_out, requiring explicit handling whenever nonempty) as a potential major KnowledgeOS capability recording input/transformation/output/preserved/lost/added-inference/confidence/provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture is not merely structure. It is: Structure + Meaning + History + Evidence + Constraints + Governance ... Transformation must preserve critical semantics
b_rows_sample.statement: States Step 218's verdict: architecture is not merely structure but Structure+Meaning+History+Evidence+Constraints+Governance, and for knowledge-centric AI systems, transformation must preserve critical semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claude must NOT: invent missing facts; merge concepts prematurely; rewrite history ... treat Gītā analogy as engineering proof ... Claude MUST: extract; classify; preserve chronology; preserve contradictions ... MASTER EVIDENCE LEDGER v0.1
b_rows_sample.statement: Previews Step 219 as the first actual evidence-audit pass over Steps 1-182, with an explicit seven-item prohibition list (no inventing facts, no premature concept merging, no rewriting history, no assuming current architecture was always intended, no treating AI interpretation as evidence or Gita analogy as engineering proof, no resolving contradictions without evidence) and a ten-item requirement list, producing a Master Evidence Ledger v0.1 as the basis for answering what was actually built, discovered and proven across Steps 1-182 -- stated to determine the final architecture and book, not the reverse.

a_rows_sample.anchor: its three central objects -- K, T and the invariants -- are mutually circular with no base case, so a knowledge state cannot be constructed, so a transition cannot be evaluated, so nothing can be computed, so nothing can be tested. And the question that would break the circle was asked at Step 005 a
a_rows_sample.statement: The central finding of the entire gap-map programme: KnowledgeOS's three central objects K, T and the invariants are mutually circular with no base case (T->K->Invariants->T, and K->Invariants->K directly), meaning a knowledge state cannot be constructed, a transition cannot be evaluated, nothing can be computed, and nothing can be tested -- and the specific question that would break this circle was asked as far back as Step 005 and remains open 235 steps later at Step 240.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T -> K -> Invariants -> T. K -> Invariants -> K (direct self-reference). ... I_3 = Status(E,K) references K while defining K. Four distinct cycles detected. No base case exists in any of them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed cycle detection over the corpus's own verbatim definitions finds mathbb K = {(G,sigma,theta,lambda,pi) | state satisfies the domain invariants} (SS232.1) whose invariants I1..I5 (SS232.39) are 4/5 functions of T (which itself requires mathbb K as domain/codomain), and I3=Status(E,K) directly references K while defining K -- four distinct cycles detected, none with a base case.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FOUNDATIONAL -- C, E, A, P. ... They are the theory's actual foundation -- not K, which the corpus places first. ... UNDEFINED -- ten objects referenced but never defined: Assessment, CriticalSemantics, Recoverable, Graph, Types, Propositions, Probability, Time, X, tau. Plus Equality on K.
a_rows_sample.statement: The dependency analysis classifies every object: FOUNDATIONAL (Context, Evidence, Authority, Policy depend on nothing unresolved -- the theory's actual foundation, not K which the corpus places first); DERIVED (L, G, SI, Assurance, Validation, Model-F-K, all definable given the foundational set, except L=History(T) which inherits T's circularity AND fails at t=0); UNDEFINED (ten objects referenced but never defined anywhere: Assessment, CriticalSemantics, Recoverable, Graph, Types, Propositions, Probability, Time, X, tau; plus Equality on K, which has no dependencies and no definition anywhere across 240 steps).

a_rows_sample.anchor: components instantiable: 1 of 6 >>> State0 CANNOT BE CONSTRUCTED >>> THEORY GAP: TRANSITION NOT COMPUTABLE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executed instantiation attempt (construct State_0 in mathbb K using only corpus definitions, then compute T(State_0)) finds only 1 of 6 components instantiable: G (knowledge graph) FAILS -- node/edge types never given for the state's graph (SS230.13's typed graph is a different, lineage, object; sigma (epistemic status) FAILS -- eleven competing value sets, none designated; theta (temporal validity) SUCCEEDS via step-185's bitemporal T_valid x T_known; lambda (lineage) PARTIAL -- History(T)=empty at t=0, external provenance unrepresentable; pi (policy) FAILS -- present in 153/182 steps but never formally typed; the membership test itself FAILS due to circularity -- State_0 cannot be constructed, and the transition is verifiably not computable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G1 -- STEP 005: What is the mathematical object being aggregated? ... closes using K in Value(e|K,I,P) without ever having defined it. ... G1 is open for 235 steps and everything downstream depends on it.
a_rows_sample.statement: The first load-bearing gap G1 is traced to Step 005, which poses exactly the right question in its title ('what is the mathematical object being aggregated'), correctly boxes Evidence!=Support!=Belief!=Probability!=Truth, but then closes using K in Value(e|K,I,P) without ever defining K -- the identical question is restated verbatim 225 steps later (SS230.49, Step 231's six inadequate models, Step 232's untyped seventh structure), meaning G1 has been open for 235 steps with everything downstream depending on it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G1 Step 005 K never defined -> enables G2 sigma has no designated value set -> enables G3 Equality on K undefined -> blocks Merge, Supersede, Remove -> enables G4 K/T/Invariants CIRCULAR -> enables G5 State0 not constructible -> enables G6 ZERO empirical validation. The minimum set whose resolution
a_rows_sample.statement: A complete dependency-aware gap chain is constructed: G1 (Step 005, K never defined) enables G2 (sigma's undesignated value set) enables G3 (undefined equality on K, blocking 3 of 9 algebra operations) enables G4 (K/T/Invariants circularity) enables G5 (State_0 not constructible, transition not computable) enables G6 (zero empirical validation in 240 steps) -- the minimum resolving set is {G1,G2,G3}; G4-G6 are consequences, not independent defects, and resolving G1 alone does not suffice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This reorders priority. The newest problems (232's untyped K, 222's non-composing SI) are symptoms. Step 005 is more important than Step 232.
a_rows_sample.statement: A major reordering of priority follows from the gap chain: the newest-discovered problems (Step 232's untyped mathbb K, Step 222's non-composing SI) are symptoms of the much older Step-005 gap, not independent root causes -- Step 005 is more important to resolve than Step 232.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ontology two competing kernel lineages ... K UNDEFINED G1 ... T circular G4 ... Epistemic status 11 competing vocabularies G2 ... Algebra 4 of 9 operations typed G3 ... Empirical validation NONE G6 one ls + one grep count empirical acts (0).
a_rows_sample.statement: The complete Theory Completion Matrix (19 areas x current-status/blocking-gap/required-resolution/verification-method) confirms every prior finding traces to the same small gap set: K undefined (G1), Policy untyped (G2-adjacent), Epistemic status 11 competing vocabularies (G2), Algebra only 4/9 operations typed and equality undefined (G3), T circular (G4), Computability NOT COMPUTABLE (G5), Empirical validation NONE (G6, 0 acts counted) -- while Temporal semantics is marked SOLVED (bitemporal, step-185) and Validation SOLVED-partially (typed as an Assessment, though Assessment itself remains undefined).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A. What is solid -- preserve, do not redesign: transformation as near-universal primitive; Provenance as I*; Bitemporality; Validation:K x X -> Assessment; T_G not closed under composition -- the best mathematics in the corpus; Evidence as admissibility condition; I_Dependency (step-080); step-175's
a_rows_sample.statement: The 'what is solid' classification names exactly ten items to preserve rather than redesign across the entire corpus: transformation (8/9 kernels), Provenance (I*), bitemporality (step-185), the Validation:K x X -> Assessment type distinction, T_G's non-closure under composition (rated the best mathematics in the corpus), evidence-as-admissibility-condition, step-080's I_Dependency (the one executable invariant), step-175's identifiability counterexample (the one reproducible witness), step-184 SS184.30's three protected transitions (most implementable AI-safety result), and the consistent mathematics-predates-Gita separation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two competing kernel lineages · E inside and beside K · I1\equiv I5 · (T,\circ) boxed as a semigroup and refuted in the same file · Model F vs the kernel on whether A lives inside K · I3=Status(E,K) defining K in terms of K.
a_rows_sample.statement: The 'semantically inconsistent' classification lists six concrete internal contradictions: the two competing kernel lineages, Evidence's double-binding (inside K and beside it), I1 being identical to I5, (T,o) boxed as both a semigroup and refuted as one in the same file, Model F vs the kernel disagreeing on whether Authority lives inside K, and I3=Status(E,K) circularly defining K in terms of K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The ~25 invariant registries with zero crosswalks; the 11 epistemic-status vocabularies; the four E-scales; the three C-scales; Identity\neq State presented as a historical finding when it appears in 0 of 182 steps.
a_rows_sample.statement: The 'merely terminology' classification identifies five categories of pure naming/vocabulary proliferation with zero reconciling crosswalks: ~25 invariant registries, 11 epistemic-status vocabularies, 4 evidence-maturity scales, 3 context-type scales, and Identity!=State being presented as a historical finding despite appearing in 0 of 182 primary steps.

a_rows_sample.anchor: G1 -> G2 -> G3, in that order. Define K; designate one epistemic-status value set; define equality on K. G4-G6 dissolve as consequences. Nothing else should be attempted first.
a_rows_sample.statement: What must be resolved first, in strict order: G1 (define K), G2 (designate one epistemic-status value set), G3 (define equality on K) -- G4 through G6 dissolve automatically as consequences once these three are fixed; nothing else should be attempted before this.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Designate K. Model D + uncertainty annotation is the strongest candidate by executed matrix -- but the corpus must choose; this remains VERIFIER RECOMMENDS. ... 6. Perform one empirical act. ... Steps 1-4 are definitional and could be done in a day. Step 5 is the proof they worked. Step 6 is the
a_rows_sample.statement: The minimum path to a complete theory is 6 concrete steps: (1) designate K (Model D + uncertainty annotation is the executed-matrix-strongest candidate, but remains VERIFIER RECOMMENDS, not a corpus choice), (2) pick one epistemic-status value set from the eleven (a choice, not a derivation), (3) define equality on K (unblocking 3 operations immediately), (4) break the circularity by defining mathbb K's membership condition without quantifying over T, (5) instantiate one state and compute one transition (the proof steps 1-4 worked), (6) perform one empirical act (one ls, one grep, output recorded verbatim -- the first empirical act in 240 steps) -- steps 1-4 rated achievable in a single day.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematical completeness NO. Engineering completeness NO. Empirical completeness NO. But the diagnosis is better than those three NOs suggest: the foundation (C,E,A,P) is sound, the failure is localised to {G1,G2,G3}, and all three are definitional choices rather than open research problems.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final three-completeness report: Mathematical (NO -- central objects circular, K undefined, 10 referenced-never-defined objects), Engineering (NO -- transition not computable, only ~1/3 of constructs implementable), Empirical (NO -- zero empirical acts in 240 steps) -- but explicitly framed as a more optimistic diagnosis than three NOs suggest: the foundation (C,E,A,P) is sound, the failure localizes entirely to {G1,G2,G3}, and all three are DEFINITIONAL CHOICES rather than open research problems.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Nothing in this gap map relies on Steps 236 or 239. The dependency analysis, the cycle detection and the instantiation attempt derive from Steps 005, 222, 230, 231 and 232 only -- all written before this programme's findings existed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independence is explicitly maintained and verified: this gap map excludes Steps 236 and 239 (classified CORPUS RESPONSE TO VERIFICATION per the standing fingerprint rule) from its evidence base, deriving its entire dependency analysis, cycle detection and instantiation attempt only from Steps 005, 222, 230, 231 and 232 -- all written before this verification programme's own findings existed, guaranteeing the gap map itself is uncontaminated by the feedback loop it discovered.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The objective is NOT to make the theory work. The objective is to determine, with evidence, whether it CAN be made to work without silently repairing, inventing, or retrospectively rewriting the corpus.
b_rows_sample.statement: The foundational reconstruction audit reframes the entire verification objective: not to make KnowledgeOS theory work, but to determine with evidence whether it CAN be made to work without silently repairing, inventing, or retrospectively rewriting the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. The corpus contains multiple kernel candidates and at least two competing kernel lineages. ... 10. The feedback loop between the corpus and the verification programme must now be explicitly controlled. 11. The corpus's historical evolution must not be treated as proof that its latest formulation
b_rows_sample.statement: An 11-item baseline of findings is frozen as the verified starting point (not to be weakened by later steps' stronger claims): multiple competing kernel lineages, K not unambiguously defined, downstream operators unevaluable, all three completenesses NO, competing epistemic-status vocabularies, undefined equality/identity on K, circular definitions involving K/T/validation, at least one independently confirmed mathematical error, much purported empirical validation being specification rather than execution, the corpus-verifier feedback loop requiring explicit control, and historical evolution not being proof of latest-formulation correctness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stop asking: What does the next step say? Instead ask: What is the minimum formal core that must exist for KnowledgeOS theory to be a valid theory at all? ... Do not assume beforehand that the answer is K = {(q,s,e,c,t,u)}. That is currently a verifier recommendation, NOT a corpus-established result
b_rows_sample.statement: The central question is explicitly changed from 'what does the next step say' to 'what is the minimum formal core that must exist for KnowledgeOS theory to be a valid theory at all', derived from the corpus and mathematical/engineering necessity -- and explicitly warns not to assume the verifier's own prior recommended K={(q,s,e,c,t,u)} is correct without testing it, since it remains a recommendation, not a corpus-established result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Object | Definition exists? | Type exists? | Depends on | Used by | Circular? | Computable? | Empirically tested? ... 25 objects
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 1 mandates a formal foundational dependency graph over ~25 named theory objects (K, knowledge item/proposition, epistemic status, evidence, provenance/lineage, context, temporal validity, uncertainty, identity/equality, transformation, policy, authority, validation, governance, observation, assessment, action, history/replay, invariants, requirements, satisfaction relation, composition, supersession, contradiction, missingness, unknown) via a 7-column table, requiring a mathematically usable definition test, not mere occurrence counting.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT select the newest candidate merely because it is newer. Do NOT select the candidate with the most components merely because it represents more concepts. ... ESTABLISHED / SUPPORTED / PARTIALLY SUPPORTED / UNDER-SPECIFIED / CONTRADICTED / REFUTED / VERIFIER PROPOSAL.
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 2 mandates reconstructing K from first principles across every serious candidate (10-point per-candidate checklist: source, semantics, type, constructors, equality, membership, admissible/invalid states, instantiability, component-definedness), compared on 15 mathematical criteria, explicitly forbidding selecting the newest or most-component-rich candidate by default, using a 7-value closed verdict vocabulary, output to K-CANDIDATE-COMPARISON.md.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A. equivalent, B. conservative extensions, C. refinements, D. genuinely competing ontologies, E. merely different linguistic labels. ... If no canonical vocabulary can be derived from the corpus, state: CANONICAL STATUS VOCABULARY NOT DERIVABLE FROM CORPUS. Do not invent one and call it verified.
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 3 mandates a complete epistemic-status-vocabulary crosswalk before any canonical vocabulary may be proposed, classifying the relationship between competing vocabularies into 5 categories (equivalent, conservative extension, refinement, genuinely competing ontology, merely different label), with an explicit fallback statement 'CANONICAL STATUS VOCABULARY NOT DERIVABLE FROM CORPUS' if none can be derived -- forbidding inventing one and calling it verified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1=K2 ... x\in K ... two knowledge items to be identical ... two states to have the same semantic content. These concepts MUST NOT be conflated. ... structural equality, semantic equality, observational equivalence, identity, version identity. ... This section must contain actual formal definitions,
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 4 mandates formally defining (or proving impossible to define) 5 distinct equality/identity notions (structural, semantic, observational equivalence, identity, version identity) that must never be conflated, then determining which equality is actually required by each of Replay/Merge/Supersede/Diff/Transition/Provenance/Validation -- requiring actual formal definitions, not prose.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K\rightarrow T\rightarrow K ... K\rightarrow validation\rightarrow K ... K\rightarrow status(E,K)\rightarrow K ... determine whether it is genuine circularity or legitimate recursive definition; ... whether a base case exists; ... Do not repair the definition silently. ... VERIFIER PROPOSED REPAIR.
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 5 mandates a dedicated dependency-cycle audit specifically testing the exact circular constructions already found (K->T->K, K->validation->K, K->status(E,K)->K), for each determining genuine-circularity-vs-legitimate-recursion, base-case existence, termination, and fixed-point-interpretation intent -- any possible repair recorded separately and explicitly as VERIFIER PROPOSED REPAIR, never silently applied.

b_rows_sample.anchor: construct the smallest possible concrete knowledge state. Use a toy example. ... Then compute: 1. membership; ... 10. state transition. If any operation cannot be computed from the definitions, STOP and record the missing definition. Do not write pseudo-code and call it execution.
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 6 mandates constructing and actually instantiating the smallest possible concrete toy knowledge state (one proposition, evidence item, context, epistemic status, temporal validity interval, uncertainty representation, provenance relation) and computing 10 operations on it (membership, equality, contradiction, supersession, addition, removal, transformation, validation, provenance lookup, state transition), stopping and recording the exact missing definition wherever an operation cannot be computed -- pseudo-code does not count as execution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is it total? Is it partial? Is it deterministic? ... What happens when evidence is missing? ... when policy rejects the transformation? ... Construct at least one concrete transition. Execute it. Record input state, transformation, output state and all derived values.
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 7 mandates formally testing the transition function T's totality, determinism, computability, composability, identity-preservation, and typing-preservation, plus behavior under 4 named failure conditions (missing evidence, conflicting evidence, absent authority, policy rejection, validation failure), requiring at least one concrete transition to be constructed and actually executed with full input/output/derived-value recording.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine whether the theory requires a typed family such as: KnowledgeState, Transformation, Policy, Authority, Assessment, History rather than one universal kernel. ... Is this a state, a relation, an operation, an assessment, a constraint, an actor-dependent authorization, or a historical propert
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 8 mandates formally testing whether knowledge must be separated from governance into a typed family of 6 distinct object kinds (KnowledgeState, Transformation, Policy, Authority, Assessment, History) rather than forced into one universal kernel -- a DDD question as much as a mathematical one, asking of every object whether it is a state, relation, operation, assessment, constraint, actor-dependent authorization, or historical property, forbidding forcing all nouns into entities or all concepts into state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: origin -> refinement -> contradiction -> resolution -> current definition. ... RETAINED, REFINED, SUPERSEDED, REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, HISTORICAL ONLY, VERIFIER PROPOSAL. ... the proper way to preserve the evolutionary nature of the corpus without assuming newer = correct.
b_rows_sample.statement: Task 10 mandates tracing surviving foundational concepts back through the 001-240 evolution only AFTER the foundational analysis is complete, classifying each into a 7-value vocabulary (RETAINED, REFINED, SUPERSEDED, REJECTED, UNRESOLVED, HISTORICAL ONLY, VERIFIER PROPOSAL), not requiring every historical statement to survive -- the proper way to preserve the corpus's evolutionary nature without assuming newer=correct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not accept PASS/verified/falsification test/simulation/evidence-based unless an actual empirical act exists. ... If the repository contains an implementation relevant to KnowledgeOS, inspect it. If no implementation exists, say: NO IMPLEMENTATION AVAILABLE FOR EMPIRICAL VALIDATION.
b_rows_sample.statement: Empirical validation is mandated to become genuinely real: no textual PASS/verified/simulation label is accepted without an actual empirical act (exact input, command/program, output, expected vs observed result, interpretation, evidence class); the actual repository must be inspected if an implementation exists, with the explicit fallback 'NO IMPLEMENTATION AVAILABLE FOR EMPIRICAL VALIDATION' rather than manufacturing one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT conclude merely from the directory name that measure theory is part of the final theory. ... sigma-algebra, measurable space, measure, probability measure, random variable, ... If measure theory is unnecessary for the final core, state so explicitly.
b_rows_sample.statement: An explicit measure-theory audit is mandated against the corpus's own folder name 'phase_measure_theory': 12 named formal measure-theoretic concepts (sigma-algebra, measurable space, measure, probability measure, random variable, conditional probability, expectation, filtration, stochastic process, Lebesgue integration, Radon-Nikodym, Dempster-Shafer remnants) must each be checked for whether they are genuinely required/actually used/formally defined/abandoned/merely historical -- explicitly forbidding concluding measure theory is part of the final theory merely from the directory name.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mathematical ... Statistical ... DDD ... Engineering ... Empirical ... Do NOT attempt to declare the KnowledgeOS theory complete until all of the following are answered.
b_rows_sample.statement: The final decision gate requires explicit answers across 5 domains (Mathematical: 13 questions about K/equality/membership/uncertainty/provenance/transformation/computability/composition/proof; Statistical: 7 questions about randomness/uncertainty/distributions/observation/evidence/assumptions/testing; DDD: 7 questions about canonical concepts/types/grouping/relations/operations/governance/UL stability; Engineering: 8 questions about instantiability/serialization/computable-equality/executable-transformation/validation/provenance/replay/failure-representation; Empirical: 5 questions about what was executed/inspected/failed/survived/untested) before the theory may be declared complete.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do NOT solve the theory for the authors. Your job is to determine whether the theory already contains enough information to solve itself. If the corpus does not determine a unique answer, report: UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS.
b_rows_sample.statement: The most important rule: the verifier must not solve the theory FOR the authors, only determine whether the theory already contains enough information to solve itself -- reporting UNDERDETERMINED BY CORPUS where no unique answer exists, listing all valid reconstructions where several exist, and explicitly listing any new assumptions or genuinely missing mathematics required.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stop and report to supervision if you reach a point where: two candidate definitions remain equally defensible; ... a repair would materially change the theory rather than merely clarify notation. ... the exact boundary between WHAT THE KNOWLEDGEOS CORPUS ESTABLISHES and WHAT A FUTURE THEORY WOULD H
b_rows_sample.statement: The stop condition triggers supervision whenever two candidate definitions remain equally defensible, a choice requires a normative/domain decision, a definition cannot be derived from the corpus, empirical validation needs an unavailable system, or a repair would materially change (not merely clarify) the theory -- the purpose of the entire phase is establishing the exact boundary between what the KnowledgeOS corpus establishes and what a future theory would have to add, only after which the project can decide to reconstruct, amend, split, or reject parts of the theory.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'verification-foundational-reconstruction-audit-directive' POSSIBLY relates to 'theory-gap-map-001-report' (batch B0038). Note: Fifth governing verification directive (post-Step-240), directly operationalizing THEORY-GAP-MAP-001's minimum-path findings into 10 explicit numbered tasks: build a ~25-concept foundational dependency graph, reconstruct K from first principles across all candidates with a strict verdict vocabulary, solve the epistemic-status crosswalk problem, formally define equality/identity on K (with a mandatory not-conflated list), break all circular definitions with genuine-vs-legitimate-recursion classification, computationally instantiate the smallest concrete knowledge state and execute 10 operations on it, formally test the transition function's totality/determinism/composability, and test whether knowledge must be separated from governance into a typed family rather than one universal kernel -- plus a historical concept trace, a real-empirical-test requirement, a mathematics-quality gate, an explicit measure-theory audit, a 5-domain (mathematical/statistical/DDD/engineering/empirical) final decision gate, 13 named required outputs, and a governing rule that the verifier must not solve the theory FOR the authors, only determine whether the corpus already contains enough information to solve itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Lens examines the boundary between what a KnowledgeOS knowledge state represents and what it does not represent. ... What is absent, undefined, unobserved, undiscovered, unresolved, unmodelled, assumed away, or otherwise outside the current representation? ... Not represented ⇒ Does not exist ... That inference is generally invalid. ... a discipline of non-collapse.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Zero Lens's purpose: examine the boundary of what a knowledge state represents vs does not, explicitly to block the invalid inference 'not represented ⇒ does not exist'; names it a 'discipline of non-collapse' that protects distinctions ordinary information systems routinely destroy.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Zero 
eq KnowledgeElement ... Zero 
eq Dimension ... Zero 
eq Value ... Zero is a constraint on interpretation.
a_rows_sample.statement: First architectural principle: Zero must not be modelled as a domain object/knowledge element/dimension/value sitting alongside Knowledge/Dimension/Statement/Value in a hierarchy; it is a lens applied to the knowledge state (Z(K_t)) and a constraint on interpretation, not a data field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency(X)=Present / Absent / Unknown ... A conventional database often collapses B and C into: NULL. KnowledgeOS must not. ... these are different epistemic axes ... Zero is pushing us toward orthogonal semantic properties, rather than a single status field.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues a dimension's epistemic state needs several orthogonal axes (Dimension, Assessment, Value, Evidence), not one enum collapsing 'investigated-and-absent' and 'never-established' into a single NULL — giving worked contrasting examples of the same dimension under different Assessment/Value/Evidence combinations.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
NO_EVIDENCE 
eq INVALID_EVIDENCE ... NOT_ASSESSED 
eq LOW_CONFIDENCE ... coverage gap ... epistemic uncertainty ... NOT_APPLICABLE 
eq UNKNOWN
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes three further non-collapse distinctions with worked examples: no-evidence vs invalid/unreliable evidence; not-assessed (a coverage gap) vs low-confidence (an epistemic uncertainty after assessment); and not-applicable (evaluated and outside domain) vs unknown.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero tells us not to resolve the contradiction merely by selecting one value. ... Claims(Version)={c_1,c_2} with Conflict(c_1,c_2)=True ... KnowledgeOS should present both information and warn the owner rather than silently deciding which information is correct. ... Conflict \neq Unknown ... Conflict \neq Invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: When two trusted sources conflict (e.g. Version=2.69 vs 3.85), Zero requires preserving the conflict as a first-class claim set with an explicit Conflict flag rather than silently picking a winner; a conflict is itself information about the current epistemic state, distinct from both Unknown and Invalid.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The derived statement is not directly observed. It is logically produced. ... Observed -> Evidence ... Derived -> Rule + premises ... The fact that a derived value is absent does not mean the underlying condition is absent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Using a worked compliance-rule example (Version=2.69, RequiredVersion=3.85, Rule ⇒ Compliance=False), shows Zero must preserve the distinction between an observed statement (backed by Evidence) and a derived statement (backed by Rule+premises); absence of a derived value does not mean the underlying condition is absent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What semantic relationships might this sentence fail to express? ... Not expressed \neq False ... Semantically unresolved \neq Semantically absent ... one of the strongest intersections between the Sanskrit lens and Zero.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies Zero to semantic/Pāṇinian parsing: a parsed sentence (e.g. 'Nexus runs version 2.69 on RHEL 9.8') expresses only certain relationships; the parser must not manufacture unexpressed implications (e.g. a specific kernel version); states Not expressed ≠ False and Semantically unresolved ≠ Semantically absent, called one of the strongest intersections between the Sanskrit/semantic lens and Zero.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "secure" may conceal many dimensions ... Which dimensions have been compressed into the word "secure"? ... Abstraction \neq Completeness ... Compression \neq Losslessness ... documents, embeddings, summaries and AI responses are all forms of compression.
a_rows_sample.statement: A high-level word like 'secure' can legitimately compress many sub-dimensions (authentication, authorization, network exposure, vulnerabilities, encryption, dependencies, patch status, configuration) without falsifying them; states the general rules Abstraction ≠ Completeness and Compression ≠ Losslessness, explicitly warning that documents, embeddings, summaries and AI responses are all forms of compression subject to this rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I found no evidence of an undocumented dependency. ... NoEvidence \Rightarrow NoDependency ... Zero rejects that inference. ... AI must be evaluated not only on: What did it extract? but also: What did it fail to discover?
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies Zero to AI evaluation specifically: an AI's 'no evidence found' must not be interpreted as 'no dependency exists'; argues AI systems must be evaluated on what they failed to discover, not only on what they extracted, calling this a fundamentally different evaluation problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Dimension discovery / Value determination / Relationship discovery / Derivation / Contradiction detection / Assumption detection / Coverage analysis / Lens variation ... TryBest = Maximize justified knowledge expansion while preserving unresolved boundaries
a_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the instruction 'try your best' into eight concrete sub-disciplines (dimension discovery, value determination, relationship discovery, derivation, contradiction detection, assumption detection, coverage analysis, lens variation), summarized as TryBest = Maximize justified knowledge expansion while preserving unresolved boundaries — explicitly contrasted with just telling an LLM to 'be comprehensive'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Every lens must be accompanied by an explicit examination of its blind spots. ... Normal lens: L_i(O) -> D_i ... Zero: Z(L_i,O) -> Boundary(L_i) ... Are there dimensions outside security that affect the security determination?
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Zero as a meta-lens applied to every other lens: a normal lens L_i(O) -> D_i must be paired with Z(L_i,O) -> Boundary(L_i), i.e. every lens must be examined for what it systematically fails to see, what assumptions it makes, and what dimensions lie outside its scope — guarding against e.g. '100 security dimensions found' being mistaken for 'security is comprehensively understood'.

type_signature.domain: a lens L_i applied to observation O

a_rows_sample.anchor: Known gap: d \in D^*\setminus D_t ... Unknown gap: D^*\setminus D_t is itself partially unknown. That is the deepest form of Zero. ... Zero(K_t) may itself contain unresolved structure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes a 'known gap' (a specific missing dimension d ∈ D*\D_t is identified) from an 'unknown gap' (D*\D_t is itself partially unknown, i.e. we don't know which dimensions are missing), and generalizes this to recursive uncertainty about unknown dimensions, unknown relationships, and unknown interpretations — concluding Zero(K_t) may itself contain unresolved structure and therefore should not be an ordinary database field.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Mithya 
eq Asat ... Appearing/not independently concrete ≠ nonexistent. ... Representation 
eq Reality ... Model insufficiency 
eq Reality insufficiency ... a powerful Zero safeguard against reification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Translates the philosophical Mithya≠Asat distinction into a Zero safeguard against reification: Representation ≠ Reality, Model insufficiency ≠ Reality insufficiency — a missing dimension in the model does not mean the corresponding aspect of the observed object does not exist, nor does difficulty establishing a statement mean the underlying phenomenon is unreal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Dimension,Value,Context,Time) at minimum. ... NotCurrentlyTrue \Rightarrow WasNeverTrue ... PreviouslyUnknown \Rightarrow PreviouslyNonexistent ... essential for knowledge history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero to temporal knowledge: a Claim must minimally carry (Dimension, Value, Context, Time); Zero must block both 'not currently true ⇒ was never true' and 'previously unknown ⇒ previously nonexistent', framed as essential for knowledge history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not create a `Zero` aggregate. Instead, Zero should influence the ubiquitous language and invariants around knowledge. ... An unassessed dimension must not be interpreted as absent. ... A representation must not be treated as the observed reality.
a_rows_sample.statement: From a DDD standpoint, explicitly rules out a 'Zero' aggregate/entity; instead Zero should shape the ubiquitous language and invariants across Observation/Dimension/Statement/Claim/Value/Evidence/Source/Assessment/Derivation/Conflict/Uncertainty/Coverage/Assumption/Context/Validity/TemporalValidity, listing five example invariants (unassessed≠absent, absence-of-evidence≠evidence-of-absence, unresolved≠false, derived statements retain derivation basis, representation≠observed reality).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ZI-01 — Non-collapse of absence: Unknown ≠ Absent ... ZI-06 — Non-collapse of dimension/value: UnknownDimension ≠ UnknownValue ... ZI-10 — Non-collapse of completeness: NoKnownGap ≠ Complete
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents a formal ten-item invariant catalog ZI-01..ZI-10 (Non-collapse of: absence Unknown≠Absent; assessment NotAssessed≠LowConfidence; applicability NotApplicable≠Unknown; evidence NoEvidence≠InvalidEvidence; interpretation Unresolved≠False; dimension/value UnknownDimension≠UnknownValue; representation/reality Model≠Reality; state/time PreviouslyUnknown≠PreviouslyAbsent; conflict Conflict≠Invalidity; completeness NoKnownGap≠Complete), flagging ZI-10 as especially important.

a_rows_sample.anchor: |D_t|/|D^*| is not a useful completeness measure. ... Coverage(K,U) = |D_{assessed}|/|D_U| ... provided D_U is explicitly defined. ... Completeness requires a defined universe of discourse.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects |D_t|/|D*| as a completeness measure when |D*|=∞ (e.g. 'KnowledgeOS knows 95%' is meaningless globally), and instead proposes a bounded-domain Coverage(K,U) = |D_assessed|/|D_U| valid only when D_U (the universe of discourse) is explicitly defined; states 'completeness requires a defined universe of discourse' as a mathematically important restriction.

type_signature.domain: knowledge state K, bounded domain U

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not: "We don't know anything." Nor: "Knowledge is impossible." It is: "Do not claim more than the represented epistemic state justifies." ... Zero actually enables more aggressive knowledge discovery.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly distinguishes Zero from epistemic pessimism: Zero does not claim knowledge is impossible or that nothing is known; it only forbids claiming more than the represented state justifies — and argues this actually enables MORE aggressive knowledge discovery, since the system can safely mark a dimension unknown and keep searching rather than prematurely declaring non-existence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CURRENT KNOWLEDGE -> ZERO EXAMINATION -> Missing values/Missing dimensions/Hidden assumptions -> More evidence/New lenses/Model challenge -> RE-EVALUATE -> NEW KNOWLEDGE -> Zero again ... Zero is recursive. It does not run once during ingestion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an operational, recursive 'Zero cycle': current knowledge -> Zero examination (missing values / missing dimensions / hidden assumptions) -> remediation (more evidence / new lenses / model challenge) -> re-evaluate -> new knowledge -> Zero again; explicitly states Zero is continuously applicable, not a one-time ingestion-time check.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Zero Lens is an epistemic and architectural discipline that examines the boundary of a knowledge state ... while explicitly preventing those conditions from being interpreted as non-existence, falsity, invalidity, irrelevance or completeness. ... Zero is the lens that prevents the domain model from turning epistemic absence into a domain fact. ... ZERO PRINCIPLE: What is not represented is not thereby nonexistent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the document's final formal definition of the Zero Lens, a one-line DDD formulation ('Zero is the lens that prevents the domain model from turning epistemic absence into a domain fact'), and a capstone 'ZERO PRINCIPLE' ('What is not represented is not thereby nonexistent') with a restated set of seven boxed non-collapse rules, concluding Zero is 'not a model of nothingness, but a rigorous discipline for preserving the boundary between what the system knows, what it has not established, and what it has not even yet learned to ask.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: The deepest insight: Zero is about non-collapse. ... Do not infer more from absence of representation than the evidence permits.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies non-collapse (do not infer more from representational absence than the evidence permits) as the deepest and most defensible part of the Zero Lens concept, deeper than the word 'boundary' itself.

b_notations: Do not collapse semantically distinct boundary conditions merely because they share a coarse projection

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.50 (shared tokens: ['collapse', 'non', 'zero'])
